records.title: Free or reduced-fee hunting and fishing license
records.summary: Arizona gives a complimentary hunting and fishing license to Veterans with a permanent 100 percent service-connected disability, and a reduced-fee license to Veterans with a lower service-connected rating. One year of Arizona residency is required either way.
records.amount: Free at 100 percent. Up to 25 percent off otherwise.
eligibility: You have lived in Arizona for one year or more immediately before you apply
You receive US government compensation for a service-connected disability
A permanent service-connected disability rated 100 percent disabling qualifies for a complimentary license
Any other service-connected disability qualifies for a license at up to 25 percent below the full fee
details: The one-year Arizona residency requirement applies to both versions and is separate from your VA rating.
Issued by the Arizona Game and Fish Department, which asks for a copy of your VA benefits letter.
If the VA certifies your 100 percent rating as permanent and not subject to reevaluation, you do not have to recertify at renewal.
records.agency: Arizona Game and Fish Department

records.title: Property tax exemption for Veterans with a service-connected disability
records.summary: If the VA rates you 100 percent service-connected disabled, your property is fully exempt from Arizona property tax. Below 100 percent, you get a partial exemption scaled to your rating.
records.amount: Fully exempt at 100 percent. Below that, scaled to your rating.
eligibility: You are a Veteran discharged, separated, or released under honorable conditions from the uniformed services
The VA has assigned you a service-connected disability rating
A 100 percent rating exempts the property entirely
Below 100 percent, the exemption is the statutory amount multiplied by your rating percentage
Income and property assessment limits apply, and both are adjusted every year
details: The statute sets a base exemption amount of $4,188, which the Arizona Department of Revenue adjusts every year for inflation. The current year's figure is higher than the number written in the statute, so confirm the exact amount with your county assessor before you rely on it.
This is claimed through your county assessor, not through the state. Deadlines are set at the county level.

Arizona has amended this exemption more than once in recent sessions, including changes to how it applies to a primary residence at a 100 percent rating. Check the current statute text if your situation is close to the line.
records.agency: Arizona Department of Revenue, administered by county assessors

records.title: Military Family Relief Fund
records.summary: Arizona pays need-based financial assistance of up to $20,000 per family to service members and families affected by a death, wound, injury, or serious illness connected to military service.
records.amount: Up to $20,000 per family, based on financial need
eligibility: The service member was killed, wounded, injured, or became seriously ill, with separate subaccounts for service after September 11, 2001 and on or before that date

An Arizona connection is required: deployed from an Arizona military base, claimed Arizona as home of record, was in the Arizona National Guard at deployment, or established residency with proof of at least twelve continuous months of physical presence in Arizona before applying
Assistance is based on demonstrated financial need resulting from the military service
details: Covered uses include stipends for living expenses for up to six months for families of those killed in combat, temporary housing and medical travel for families of hospitalized service members, and other living expenses the committee approves.
IMPORTANT: the statute establishes this fund through December 31, 2026. Check whether the Legislature has extended it before relying on it.
The fund is made up of private donations, grants, and bequests, so available money varies.
records.agency: Arizona Department of Veterans' Services

records.title: Military retirement pay is fully exempt from Arizona income tax
records.summary: Arizona does not tax military retired or retainer pay. Since the 2021 tax year the full amount is subtracted from your Arizona gross income, with no cap.
records.amount: Full amount, no cap, from tax year 2021 onward
eligibility: You receive retired or retainer pay from the uniformed services of the United States
Uniformed services includes the US military, the Public Health Service Commissioned Corps, and the NOAA Commissioned Officer Corps
There is no disability rating requirement and no income test
details: The cap was removed in stages. Through 2018 the subtraction was capped at $2,500, for 2019 and 2020 it was $3,500, and from the 2021 tax year onward it is the full amount received.
This is a subtraction on your Arizona return, so you have to claim it. It is not automatic.
Arizona separately does not tax active duty military pay.
records.agency: Arizona Department of Revenue

records.title: Tuition waiver scholarship at Arizona public colleges and universities
records.summary: Arizona waives tuition at its public universities and community colleges for Purple Heart recipients rated at least 50 percent disabled, and for the children and surviving spouses of service members killed in the line of duty.
records.amount: Full tuition, up to 64 credit hours at a community college
eligibility: Purple Heart recipient from the US armed forces with a VA disability rating of 50 percent or more
Or a National Guard member awarded a Purple Heart after September 11, 2001
Or the child, age 30 or younger, or the unmarried surviving spouse of a service member or first responder killed in the line of duty or who died of line-of-duty injuries
Or the child or unmarried surviving spouse of an Arizona resident Veteran or service member who suffered a post-traumatic stress injury in the line of duty and died by suicide
Purple Heart recipients with a felony conviction are not eligible
details: The same statute also covers dependents of peace officers, firefighters, correctional officers, emergency paramedics, and National Guard members killed in the line of duty.
Apply through the financial aid office of the Arizona public university or community college you plan to attend.
records.agency: Arizona Board of Regents and the community college districts

records.title: Arizona State Veteran Homes
records.summary: Arizona operates skilled nursing and long-term care homes for Veterans. The Department of Veterans Services is authorized by statute to build and run them and sets the admission rules and resident charges.
eligibility: Admission rules and resident charges are set by the Department of Veterans Services, not fixed in statute
Contact the Department directly to check eligibility and current waiting lists
details: The statute authorizes the Department to acquire property for, construct, and operate Veterans home facilities in Arizona. The detailed admission criteria live in administrative rule rather than in the statute, so the Department is the place to confirm them.
Homes operate in Phoenix and Tucson, with additional homes in Flagstaff and Yuma. Confirm current locations and availability with the Department.
records.agency: Arizona Department of Veterans' Services

records.title: Vehicle license tax and registration fee exemption
records.summary: Veterans certified by the VA at 100 percent disability and drawing compensation on that basis pay no vehicle license tax and no registration fees on one vehicle.
records.amount: No vehicle license tax or registration fees on one vehicle
eligibility: The VA has certified you as 100 percent disabled and you are drawing compensation on that basis
Covers one personally owned vehicle, or a vehicle you own with another party, and any replacement of it
You must show satisfactory proof of the certification when you first register the vehicle
A surviving spouse keeps the exemption until remarriage or death
details: This covers one vehicle at a time. Replacing that vehicle carries the exemption over; adding a second vehicle does not.
Handled by the Arizona Department of Transportation Motor Vehicle Division at registration.
records.agency: Arizona Department of Transportation, Motor Vehicle Division

records.title: Arizona Veterans' Memorial Cemeteries
records.summary: Arizona establishes and operates state cemeteries for Veterans, and provides burial services there for Arizona National Guard and US Armed Forces Reserve members discharged under honorable conditions.
eligibility: Veterans, under the Department of Veterans Services rules
Members of the Arizona National Guard whose service was terminated under honorable conditions
Members of the United States armed forces reserves whose service was terminated under honorable conditions
details: The statute authorizes the Department to acquire property for, establish, and operate cemeteries for Veterans in Arizona, and specifically to provide burial services for Guard and Reserve members separated under honorable conditions.
State cemeteries operate at Sierra Vista, Camp Navajo near Flagstaff, and Marana north of Tucson. Confirm current locations and eligibility with the Department before making arrangements.
records.agency: Arizona Department of Veterans' Services

records.title: Veterans preference points in state and local government hiring
records.summary: Arizona adds preference points to your merit-system exam grade for state and local government jobs: five points for a Veteran, ten if you have a service-connected disability.
records.amount: 5 points, or 10 points with a service-connected disability
eligibility: You are a Veteran of the armed forces taking a merit-system employment exam for the state or a political subdivision
You must earn a passing grade without the preference first, then the points are added
A service-connected disability raises the preference to ten points
A spouse or surviving spouse of a Veteran who died of a service-connected disability gets the five-point preference
details: The points are added to a passing grade. They do not turn a failing exam into a passing one.
This applies to Arizona state government and to political subdivisions such as counties and cities that use a merit system.
The same statute gives a five-point preference to a person with a disability, separate from Veteran status.
records.agency: Arizona Department of Administration and local merit systems

records.title: CalVet home loan for Veterans and active duty service members
records.summary: California runs its own home and farm loan program for Veterans through the Veterans' Farm and Home Purchase Act. It is a state program, separate from the federal VA home loan guaranty.
eligibility: Any Veteran as defined in Military and Veterans Code 980, which generally requires qualifying wartime or designated-period service and an honorable discharge or release under honorable conditions
Or any person currently on active duty in the military or naval service of the United States who meets the other qualifications in section 980

Section 980 also covers Reserve and National Guard members called to and released from active duty during periods a presidential executive order specifies the United States is engaged in combat or homeland defense
People separated under dishonorable conditions, separated because of alienage, or whose service was training only are excluded
details: The stated object of the article is to provide Veterans with the opportunity to acquire farms and homes.
Terms, rates, loan limits, and property requirements are set by the California Department of Veterans Affairs and change over time. Get current terms directly from CalVet before you shop for a house.
This is not the federal VA loan. Do not assume a rule you read about the federal program carries over to CalVet, and ask specifically how the two interact if you are eligible for both.
The eligibility definition in section 980 is detailed and period-specific. If your service dates are near a boundary, have a County Veterans Service Officer read the statute against your DD-214.
records.agency: California Department of Veterans Affairs (CalVet)
records.statuteRef: Cal. Mil. & Vet. Code 987.52, definition at Cal. Mil. & Vet. Code 980

records.title: College Fee Waiver for the children and spouses of disabled or deceased Veterans
records.summary: California waives system-wide tuition and fees at UC, CSU, and community colleges for certain dependents of Veterans with a service-connected disability or who died in service. Most categories carry an income test.
eligibility: A child of a Veteran who has a service-connected disability, was killed in service, or died of a service-connected disability, if the child's annual income including parental support is below the state poverty level figure named in the statute
A dependent, or an unmarried surviving spouse, of a California National Guard member killed or permanently disabled in the line of duty while in the active service of the state

An undergraduate who is a Medal of Honor recipient, or a child age 27 or younger of a Medal of Honor recipient, subject to the same income test and a California residency requirement for the recipient
details: The waiver covers system-wide fees at a University of California campus, a California State University campus, or a California Community College. The statute conditions University of California participation on action by the Regents.

The income test is written as annual household income below the amount calculated for a single person with no dependents under Revenue and Taxation Code 18501. That figure changes, so ask the county veterans service office to run your numbers rather than guessing.

Applications are handled through your County Veterans Service Office, not the college financial aid office. There are several plans under this program with different rules, so bring your DD-214 and the Veteran's VA rating letter to the appointment.
records.agency: California Department of Veterans Affairs, through County Veterans Service Offices

records.title: Disabled Veteran Business Enterprise participation in state contracts
records.summary: California sets a participation goal for certified Disabled Veteran Business Enterprises on state contracts. Certifying your business makes it easier for state agencies and their prime contractors to award you work.
records.amount: The statute states a DVBE participation goal of a minimum of 3 percent of total contract value.
eligibility: A sole proprietorship at least 51 percent owned by one or more disabled Veterans, or the comparable ownership structure for a corporation or joint venture
One or more disabled Veterans control the management and daily business operations
The home office is located in the United States and is not a branch or subsidiary of a foreign corporation or other foreign entity
details: This is a participation goal placed on state procurement, not a guaranteed award. It creates a reason for agencies and prime contractors to seek you out once you are certified.
Certification is handled by the Department of General Services Office of Small Business and DVBE Services. Certification is a separate step from registering as a state vendor.
Military and Veterans Code 999 also carries substantial penalties for fraudulent DVBE claims. Read the certification requirements carefully before you file.
records.agency: California Department of General Services, Office of Small Business and DVBE Services

records.title: Disabled Veteran license plates from the DMV
records.summary: California issues special Disabled Veteran license plates with no additional plate fee. A county veterans service officer or the VA can certify your disability instead of a physician.
eligibility: You meet the Vehicle Code definition of disabled Veteran, which requires a disability from injury or disease suffered on active service with the armed forces
Qualifying conditions include a disability rated at 100 percent by the VA or the service branch for a diagnosed disease or disorder that substantially impairs mobility

Also qualifying: a disability so severe that you cannot move without an assistive device, the loss or loss of use of one or more limbs, or permanent blindness as defined in Welfare and Institutions Code 19153
details: Vehicle Code 5007 says the department issues these plates without additional fees.

For Disabled Veteran plates the DMV must accept a certificate from a county veterans service officer, the California Department of Veterans Affairs, or the United States Department of Veterans Affairs in place of the physician's certificate that other applicants have to supply.

The Vehicle Code definition of disabled Veteran in section 295.7 is narrower than a general VA service-connected rating. A rating below 100 percent does not qualify unless one of the other listed conditions applies to you.
Separate rules govern vehicle registration fee exemptions. Ask the DMV directly about registration fees rather than assuming the plate rule covers them.
records.agency: California Department of Motor Vehicles
records.statuteRef: Cal. Veh. Code 5007, definition at Cal. Veh. Code 295.7

records.title: Disabled Veterans' property tax exemption on your home
records.summary: California exempts a large slice of the assessed value of your principal residence if the VA rates you 100 percent disabled, pays you at the 100 percent rate for unemployability, or you are blind in both eyes or have lost the use of two or more limbs. A bigger exemption applies if your household income is under the annual limit.
records.amount: For the 2026 lien date, $180,671 of assessed value, or $271,009 if household income is $81,131 or less.
eligibility: The VA or your branch of service rates you 100 percent disabled, or compensates you at the 100 percent rate because a service-connected disability leaves you unable to hold substantially gainful employment
Or you are blind in both eyes, meaning visual acuity of 5/200 or less, or a visual field contracted to 5 degrees or less
Or you have lost the use of two or more limbs, by amputation or through ankylosis, progressive muscular dystrophy, or paralysis
Your character of discharge was under other than dishonorable conditions
You served during one of the time periods listed in Revenue and Taxation Code 205.5(b)(1)(A)
The property is your principal place of residence
The larger low-income exemption applies only if annual household income is at or below the limit, which is $81,131 for the 2026 lien date

An unmarried surviving spouse may claim it if the Veteran qualified during their lifetime, would have qualified had they been alive on January 1, 1977, or died from a service-connected injury or disease
details: The dollar figures move every year. Revenue and Taxation Code 205.5 sets a base of $100,000, a low-income amount of $150,000 and a $40,000 household income limit, then compounds all three annually by a California Consumer Price Index factor measured February to February.

The 2026 figures above are from Board of Equalization Letter to Assessors 2025/014, issued 21 May 2025. It applied a factor of 1.03065, a 3.065 percent rise, to the 2025 amounts of $175,298 basic, $262,950 low-income, and a $78,718 income limit.

That letter is the thing to watch, not the county. The Board issues one each spring setting the amounts for the next lien date, so a single document a year covers this benefit. They are listed under Letters to Assessors on boe.ca.gov.
This exemption is worth more than the Veterans' Exemption and the Homeowners' Exemption. If you qualify for more than one, claim this one.
A 100 percent VA rating is enough on its own. The Board instructs assessors to treat the rating letter as sufficient and not to ask for medical files.
Claim it on form BOE-261-G from your county assessor, with proof of the disability rating and proof that your character of service was other than dishonorable, such as a DD-214.

First year deadline: file between the eligibility event and the following January 1, or 90 days after the event, whichever is later, to get the whole exemption. File later and you get 85 percent for that first year.

The basic exemption never has to be refiled. The low-income exemption does, every year between January 1 and February 15 for the full amount. February 16 through December 10 gets 90 percent, and after December 10 gets 85 percent.
If you are confined to a hospital or a care facility, the home still counts as your principal residence, as long as it is not rented or leased to anyone.
If two qualified claimants own the home together, each gets the exemption to the extent of their own interest in it.
records.agency: California State Board of Equalization, administered by county assessors

records.title: Partial state income tax exclusion for military retirement pay
records.summary: California now lets qualified taxpayers leave up to $20,000 of federal uniformed services retirement pay out of state gross income. There is a federal adjusted gross income ceiling, and the provision expires after tax year 2029.
records.amount: Up to $20,000 of retirement pay per year, for tax years 2025 through 2029.
eligibility: You receive retirement pay from the federal government for service in the uniformed services

The statute defines uniformed services as the Armed Forces, the Army National Guard and Air National Guard when engaged in active duty for training, inactive duty training, or full-time National Guard duty, the commissioned corps of the Public Health Service, and the NOAA Commissioned Officer Corps
Federal adjusted gross income of $250,000 or less for a surviving spouse, or for spouses filing a joint return
Federal adjusted gross income of $125,000 or less for anyone else
The income test uses the adjusted gross income shown on your federal return for the same tax year
details: This is new. It was added by SB 132, Stats. 2025, Ch. 17, effective 27 June 2025, so tax year 2025 returns are the first ones that can claim it.

It applies to taxable years beginning on or after 1 January 2025 and before 1 January 2030, and the section repeals itself on 1 December 2030. Unless the Legislature extends it, tax year 2029 is the last one.

A companion section, Revenue and Taxation Code 17132.10, gives a separate $20,000 exclusion for Survivor Benefit Plan annuity payments received by a surviving spouse or other named beneficiary. Same income ceilings, same 2025 through 2029 window, same repeal date. The plan is the Department of Defense one under 10 U.S.C. 1447 to 1455.
This is an exclusion you claim on your California return. It is not automatic, and it changes nothing on your federal return.

The cap is a flat $20,000 in the statute with no inflation adjustment, so it does not rise year to year. Check the Franchise Tax Board instructions for the year you are filing in case the Legislature amends it.
records.agency: California Franchise Tax Board

records.title: Professional license renewal fees waived during active duty
records.summary: If you held a valid license from a California Department of Consumer Affairs board when you were called to active duty, the board must waive renewal fees and continuing education while you serve. There are strict notice deadlines after you are discharged.
eligibility: You held a current and valid license or registration with the board at the time you were called to active duty
The waiver runs only for the period you are on active duty service
You give the board written documentation substantiating your active duty service
Active duty includes service in the United States Armed Forces and California National Guard duty, including duty under a state emergency proclamation
details: The waiver covers renewal fees, continuing education requirements, and other renewal requirements while you are on active duty.

Two deadlines matter after you separate. You must notify the board of your discharge within 60 days of receiving your notice of discharge, and you must meet all necessary renewal requirements within six months.
This applies to boards within the Department of Consumer Affairs as defined in Business and Professions Code section 22. Contact your specific board, since each one handles the paperwork differently.
This is a benefit tied to active duty service, not to Veteran status by itself. Separate expedited licensure rules exist for Veterans and military spouses, so ask your board about those as well.
records.agency: California Department of Consumer Affairs licensing boards

records.title: Reduced-fee sport fishing license for disabled Veterans
records.summary: Honorably discharged Veterans rated 50 percent or more service-connected disabled can buy a California sport fishing license at a steeply reduced fee. You have to prequalify with the Department of Fish and Wildlife first.
eligibility: Honorable discharge from the United States armed forces
Service-connected disability rating of 50 percent or greater
The reduced-fee disabled Veteran license is available to residents and nonresidents
details: You must prequalify before you can buy the license. Send the Department of Fish and Wildlife documentation from the United States Department of Veterans Affairs verifying your discharge status and your disability rating.

The CDFW page listed the disabled Veteran sport fishing license at $10.04 at a CDFW office and $10.54 through a license agent. License fees are reset every year, so treat those as illustrative and check the current price before you buy.
This covers the base sport fishing license. Report cards and validations for salmon, steelhead, sturgeon, spiny lobster, and similar species are priced separately.
records.agency: California Department of Fish and Wildlife

records.title: Veterans' preference in California state civil service hiring
records.summary: If you pass an entrance examination for a California state job, veterans' preference places you in the top rank of the resulting eligibility list. Certain spouses and surviving spouses get the same placement.
eligibility: You are a Veteran who passes the entrance examination for the position
Or you are the widow or widower of a Veteran
Or you are the spouse of a Veteran rated 100 percent disabled
Anyone dishonorably discharged or released is excluded
details: The preference works by ranking, not by adding points to your score. Qualifying applicants who pass the entrance exam are placed in the top rank of the eligibility list, which is what puts your name in front of a hiring manager.
The statute is written around entrance examinations and the resulting eligibility list. It does not by its terms extend to promotional examinations for people already in state service.
You have to claim and document the preference through CalHR. Verify your status before you apply for a job rather than after.
records.agency: California Department of Human Resources (CalHR)

records.title: State park pass for disabled Veterans and former prisoners of war
records.summary: If you are a California resident Veteran rated at least 50 percent service-connected disabled, or you were held as a prisoner of war, you can get a pass covering the state park system. It includes boat launching facilities.
eligibility: You are a California resident
You have a 50 percent or greater service-connected disability, or you were held as a prisoner of war
You were honorably discharged
You provide proof of eligibility to the department
details: The statute says the pass admits the bearer to all facilities in units of the state park system, including boat launching facilities.
Apply through California State Parks. Bring your VA rating letter and your DD-214 or other discharge document.
Confirm what the pass covers at the specific park you plan to visit. Some concession-operated facilities inside state parks charge separately.
records.agency: California Department of Parks and Recreation

records.title: Admission to the Veterans Homes of California
records.summary: California operates eight Veterans Homes offering long-term care, assisted living, adult day health, and independent living. Eligible spouses and domestic partners can be admitted alongside a Veteran.
eligibility: Aged or disabled persons who served in the Armed Forces of the United States and were discharged or released from active duty under conditions other than dishonorable
Bona fide California resident who meets the federal VA benefit requirements referenced in the statute
A spouse or registered domestic partner of an eligible Veteran, subject to a joint residency requirement of at least one year
A surviving spouse or domestic partner of a Medal of Honor recipient or a former prisoner of war
details: The eight homes are in Yountville, Barstow, Chula Vista, West Los Angeles, Lancaster, Ventura, Fresno, and Redding.
Not every home offers every level of care. Confirm which levels of care are available at the location you are considering before you apply.

The statute establishes admission priority for Medal of Honor recipients, former prisoners of war, Veterans rated 70 percent or more service-connected disabled, and Veterans who meet needs-based criteria set by the secretary.
Residents pay a share of the cost. Fee structures depend on level of care, disability rating, and income, so ask the admissions office at the specific home for a written fee estimate.
records.agency: California Department of Veterans Affairs (CalVet)
records.statuteRef: Cal. Mil. & Vet. Code 1012, homes defined at Cal. Mil. & Vet. Code 1010

records.title: Congressman C.W. Bill Young Veteran Tuition Waiver: pay in-state rates
records.summary: Florida public colleges, universities, and career centers must waive out-of-state fees for honorably discharged Veterans who physically reside in Florida while enrolled. You pay the resident rate even if you have not yet met normal residency rules.
records.amount: Waiver of out-of-state fees. Tuition and fees cannot exceed the resident rate
eligibility: An honorably discharged Veteran of the U.S. Armed Forces, the U.S. Reserve Forces, or the National Guard who physically resides in Florida while enrolled
Or a person entitled to and using VA educational assistance for a quarter, semester, or term beginning after July 1, 2015, who physically resides in Florida while enrolled
Applies at state universities, Florida College System institutions, school district career centers under Fla. Stat. 1001.44, and charter technical career centers
details: This is a waiver of the out-of-state surcharge, not free tuition. You still owe the in-state amount, which is where your GI Bill or other aid comes in.
The waiver is established in subsection (13) of Fla. Stat. 1009.26.
Institutions are required to report annually on the waivers they grant.
Ask the school's Veteran services or registrar office to apply the waiver. It is not always applied automatically.
records.agency: Florida public postsecondary institutions

records.title: Homestead tax discount at age 65 for a combat-related disability
records.summary: At 65 or older with a combat-related permanent disability, your homestead property tax is discounted by the same percentage as your VA disability rating. A 70 percent rating means a 70 percent discount.
records.amount: A percentage discount equal to your VA permanent service-connected disability percentage
eligibility: Age 65 or older
Partially or totally permanently disabled
The disability was combat-related
Honorably discharged upon separation from military service
details: The statute reads: "The discount shall be in a percentage equal to the percentage of the veteran's permanent, service-connected disability as determined by the United States Department of Veterans Affairs."
This is a percentage discount off the tax owed, not a fixed dollar exemption, so it can be worth far more than the $5,000 exemption under Fla. Stat. 196.24.
The combat-related requirement is the part people miss. A high rating that is not combat-related does not qualify for this particular discount.

Apply to your county property appraiser by March 1. The statute names exactly three things you must submit: an official VA letter stating your service-connected disability percentage and evidence that reasonably identifies the disability as combat-related, a copy of your honorable discharge, and proof of age as of January 1 of the year the discount applies to.
Missing March 1 is not fatal. You may still apply and file a petition with the county value adjustment board under Fla. Stat. 194.011(3).

You can apply before the VA paperwork arrives. Once it does, the discount is granted back to the date of your original application and excess taxes are refunded, limited to the 4 year period in section 197.182(1)(e).
If the property appraiser denies you, they must tell you in writing with reasons by July 1, and the notice must explain your right to appeal to the value adjustment board.
The discount is applied after every other exemption. The appraiser deducts all other exemptions from assessed value first, then subtracts your disability percentage from what is left.

If the Veteran dies first, the discount carries over to a surviving spouse who holds title and lives there, until they remarry or sell. A spouse who sells can transfer a discount not exceeding the dollar amount on the most recent tax roll to a new primary residence.
records.agency: Florida county property appraisers

records.title: $5,000 property tax exemption at a 10 percent or higher wartime disability
records.summary: A Florida resident ex-servicemember discharged under honorable conditions and disabled 10 percent or more during a wartime period gets $5,000 of property value exempted from taxation. An unremarried surviving spouse is entitled to the same exemption.
records.amount: $5,000 of property value
eligibility: An ex-servicemember as defined in Fla. Stat. 196.012 who is a bona fide Florida resident
Discharged under honorable conditions
Disabled to a degree of 10 percent or more by misfortune or while serving during a period of wartime service as defined in Fla. Stat. 1.01(14)
An unremarried surviving spouse of such a disabled ex-servicemember also qualifies
details: A certificate of disability from the U.S. Government or the U.S. Department of Veterans Affairs, produced to the county property appraiser, is prima facie evidence that you are entitled to the exemption.

As with the total and permanent exemption, you may apply before you have the VA paperwork in hand. When it arrives the exemption is granted back to the date of your original application and excess taxes paid are refunded, limited to the 4 year period in section 197.182(1)(e).
This is a much smaller benefit than the full exemption under Fla. Stat. 196.081. If your disability is total and permanent, look at that one instead.
records.agency: Florida county property appraisers

records.title: Free hunting and fishing licenses at a 50 percent or higher rating
records.summary: Honorably discharged Veterans certified with a service-connected disability rating of 50 percent or greater are exempt from Florida recreational license and permit fees. The license runs 5 years and is reissued on request.
records.amount: No fee for the recreational license or permit
eligibility: A disabled Veteran of the U.S. Armed Forces honorably discharged upon separation from service
Certified by the U.S. Department of Veterans Affairs or by any branch of the U.S. Armed Forces as having a service-connected disability percentage rating of 50 percent or greater
You must show proof of that certification or determination
details: The exemption is at Fla. Stat. 379.353(1)(c). The license expires after 5 years and must be reissued on request every 5 years after that, a change effective July 1, 2024.

A separate provision, Fla. Stat. 379.353(2)(q), exempts participants in organized outdoor recreational events whose primary purpose is the rehabilitation or enjoyment of disabled Veterans with a service-connected rating of zero or higher, or of active duty or reserve servicemembers. That exemption covers the Veteran or servicemember, immediate family, and one designated assistant for the duration of the event.
Apply through the Florida Fish and Wildlife Conservation Commission or a county tax collector.
records.agency: Florida Fish and Wildlife Conservation Commission

records.title: No driver license or ID card fees at a 100 percent disability rating
records.summary: An honorably discharged Veteran with a 100 percent total and permanent service-connected disability rating is exempt from all driver license and identification card fees in Fla. Stat. 322.21. You still have to meet the normal qualifications for the license.
records.amount: All fees required by Fla. Stat. 322.21 are waived
eligibility: Honorably discharged from the Armed Forces

And either holding a valid identification card issued by the Florida Department of Veterans' Affairs under Fla. Stat. 295.17, or determined by the U.S. Department of Veterans Affairs to have a 100 percent total and permanent service-connected disability rating for compensation, or determined to have a service-connected total and permanent disability rating of 100 percent and in receipt of disability retirement pay from a branch of the U.S. Armed Services
You must otherwise be qualified to obtain a driver license under Chapter 322
details: The exemption is in subsection (7) of Fla. Stat. 322.21.
The Florida Department of Veterans' Affairs identification card issued under Fla. Stat. 295.17 is one accepted route to proving eligibility, so getting that card can be worth doing on its own.
Bring your proof to the tax collector or driver license office. Fees are not waived retroactively, so present it before you pay.
records.agency: Florida Department of Highway Safety and Motor Vehicles

records.title: State-paid education for children and spouses of deceased or 100 percent disabled servicemembers
records.summary: Florida declares it state policy to provide education at state expense to dependent children and spouses of servicemembers who died from service-connected causes or who have a 100 percent service-connected disability rating. Residency and application timing rules apply.
eligibility: A dependent child of a servicemember who died from a service-connected injury, disease, or disability, or who has a 100 percent service-connected disability rating
A spouse of a deceased servicemember who applies within 5 years of the servicemember's death
A spouse of a disabled servicemember who has been married to them for at least 1 year, with benefits available only during the marriage
Residency conditions apply, including Florida being listed as the official home of record in DEERS or otherwise qualifying as a Florida resident
details: Fla. Stat. 295.01 sets the policy. The actual award amounts, minimum requirements, and enrollment rules live in Fla. Stat. 295.03 through 295.05 and Fla. Stat. 1009.40, so read those before you count on a specific dollar figure.
The 100 percent rating can be shown through the VA, through military retirement for disability, or through a valid Florida Department of Veterans' Affairs identification card.
The 5 year application window for a surviving spouse is easy to miss. If your servicemember has died, start this early.
Related sections in Chapter 295 cover children of prisoners of war and persons missing in action, and children of servicemembers lost in specific named operations.
records.agency: Florida Department of Veterans' Affairs

records.title: Free DV license plate for a 100 percent service-connected disability
records.summary: Florida issues a free DV license plate to honorably discharged Veterans with a 100 percent service-connected disability rating, or whose vehicle was bought with VA financial assistance. Service charges still apply at registration and renewal.
records.amount: The license plate is free. Statutory service charges at initial registration and renewal still apply
eligibility: Honorably discharged from the U.S. Armed Forces
Continuous Florida residency for 5 years, or domicile established under the provisions the statute names

And one of: the vehicle was purchased with VA financial assistance, or the VA determined you have a service-connected 100 percent disability rating, or you have a 100 percent service-connected disability rating while receiving disability retirement pay
details: Proof is a valid Florida Department of Veterans' Affairs identification card, or a letter from the U.S. Department of Veterans Affairs certifying a service-connected disability rating of 100 percent.
Renewal requires a certified statement that you still qualify.
The plate must be removed when you sell the vehicle, but it can be transferred to another vehicle you own.
You may choose a military or specialty plate instead, but the statute notes those do not carry the same parking and accessibility protections that the DV plate does.
records.agency: Florida Department of Highway Safety and Motor Vehicles

records.title: No county or city permit fees for accessibility improvements to your home
records.summary: A totally and permanently disabled Veteran does not pay any county or municipal license or permit fee to make a dwelling they own habitable or safe, such as ramps or widened doors. It covers the fee, not the cost of the work.
records.amount: Any license or permit fee charged by a county or municipality for the qualifying improvement
eligibility: A Florida resident Veteran, honorably discharged, who is totally and permanently disabled

Holding a valid Florida Department of Veterans' Affairs identification card, or a 100 percent service-connected disability rating from the U.S. Department of Veterans Affairs, or military retirement pay for that disability
The dwelling is owned by the Veteran
The improvements are ramps, widening of doors, and similar improvements for the purpose of making the dwelling habitable or safe for the Veteran
details: The statute says such a Veteran is "not required to pay any license or permit fee, by whatever name known, to any county or municipality in order to make improvements upon a dwelling owned by the veteran."
The limit is the type of work. General remodeling that is not about making the home habitable or safe for you is not covered.
Raise the exemption with the county or city building department when you pull the permit, and bring your VA identification card or rating letter.
records.agency: Florida county and municipal building departments

records.title: Florida does not tax personal income, including military and VA pay
records.summary: The Florida Constitution bars a state income tax on natural persons who are residents of the state. Your military retired pay, drill pay, and VA disability compensation are not taxed by Florida.
details: Fla. Stat. 220.02(1) refers to "the mandate in s. 5, Art. VII of the State Constitution that no income tax be levied upon natural persons who are residents and citizens of this state."
Because there is no personal income tax at all, Florida has no separate military retirement pay exclusion or Veteran income tax credit. There is nothing to apply for and no form to file.

The Florida Department of Revenue lists every tax and fee it administers at floridarevenue.com/taxes/taxesfees. Corporate income, sales and use, fuel, and documentary stamp are on that list. Personal income tax is not on it at all.
Federal tax rules still apply. VA disability compensation remains non-taxable federally, and military retired pay is still federally taxable.
records.agency: Florida Department of Revenue
records.statuteRef: Fla. Const. art. VII, s. 5, as referenced in Fla. Stat. 220.02(1)

records.title: Tuition waiver for Purple Heart and superior combat decoration recipients
records.summary: Florida public institutions must waive tuition for undergraduate college credit and career certificate programs for recipients of the Purple Heart or a combat decoration superior in precedence. The waiver covers 110 percent of the credit hours the program requires.
records.amount: Tuition for 110 percent of the required credit hours of the program you are enrolled in
eligibility: You received a Purple Heart or another combat decoration superior in precedence
You are enrolled in an undergraduate college credit program or a career certificate program
You must meet the statute's criteria on enrollment status, Florida residency, and submitting documentation
details: This waiver is subsection (8) of Fla. Stat. 1009.26. It applies at state universities, Florida College System institutions, school district career centers under Fla. Stat. 1001.44, and charter technical career centers.
It is a tuition waiver, which is broader than the out-of-state fee waiver under the Bill Young program. If you qualify for both, ask the school which applies to your program.
Confirm with the institution exactly which documentation of the award they require and the residency conditions that apply to you.
records.agency: Florida public postsecondary institutions

records.title: State veterans nursing homes
records.summary: Florida operates state veterans nursing homes for Veterans who need nursing home care and are Florida residents when they apply. Service-connected disability moves you up the admission priority list.
eligibility: You are a Veteran, have eligible peacetime service, or are the spouse or surviving spouse of a Veteran
You are in need of nursing home care
You are a resident of the state at the time of application
You have no outstanding debt to the department for prior services
You apply for all available governmental financial assistance
You obtain approval from the U.S. Department of Veterans Affairs
details: Admission priority runs in this order: Florida resident Veterans eligible under state law, then Veterans with a VA-determined service-connected disability or discharged for a disability incurred in service where that disability is why care is needed, then Veterans with a non-service-connected disability who cannot afford nursing home care and swear under oath to that inability, then spouses or surviving spouses of Veterans in those categories.
The director may waive the residency requirement for evacuees from a state under a disaster emergency declaration.
Chapter 296 also covers the Veterans' Domiciliary Home of Florida under Part I and Veterans' Adult Day Health Care under Part III. If nursing home level care is more than you need, look at those.
The homes are run by the Florida Department of Veterans' Affairs. Contact them for the current list of homes, waiting lists, and cost of care.
records.agency: Florida Department of Veterans' Affairs

records.title: Full homestead property tax exemption for a total and permanent service-connected disability
records.summary: If you were honorably discharged with a service-connected total and permanent disability, the home you own and live in is exempt from property tax entirely. You prove it with the VA letter certifying total and permanent disability.
records.amount: The full ad valorem tax on your homestead
eligibility: Honorably discharged with a service-connected total and permanent disability
A letter from the United States Government or the U.S. Department of Veterans Affairs certifying that you are totally and permanently disabled
You own the real estate and use it as your homestead
You were a permanent resident of Florida on January 1 of the tax year you are claiming, or the Veteran was a permanent resident on January 1 of the year they died
details: The statute says producing the total and permanent disability letter to your county property appraiser is prima facie evidence that you are entitled to the exemption.

You can apply before the VA documentation arrives. Once you send the documentation in, the exemption is granted as of the date of your original application and excess taxes you paid are refunded, limited to the 4 year period in section 197.182(1)(e).

If the Veteran dies first, the exemption carries over to the surviving spouse for as long as they hold title, live there, and do not remarry. A spouse who sells can transfer an exemption amount not exceeding the amount on the most recent tax roll to a new primary residence.
A separate provision in the same section gives a full exemption to the surviving spouse of a Veteran who died from service-connected causes while on active duty.
If you buy a new property between January 1 and November 1, the statute provides a prorated refund path once the exemption is granted on the new property the next tax year.
This is claimed through your county property appraiser, not through a state office.
records.agency: Florida county property appraisers

records.title: Certified veteran business enterprise state contracting preference
records.summary: Florida certifies businesses at least 51 percent owned by wartime or service-disabled Veterans. When bids are equal on price, quality, and service, the state must award the contract to the certified veteran business enterprise.
eligibility: At least 51 percent owned by one or more wartime Veterans or service-disabled Veterans
Management and daily business operations controlled by qualifying Veterans, or by the spouse or permanent caregiver in the case of a Veteran with a permanent total disability
Independently owned and operated
200 or fewer full-time employees
Net worth of $5 million or less
Doing business in Florida
details: The preference is a tie-breaker. State agencies must award to the certified veteran business enterprise when bids are equal with respect to all relevant considerations, including price, quality, and service.
If more than one preference-eligible business submits an equal bid, the contract goes to the one with the smallest net worth.
Political subdivisions are encouraged, not required, to give similar consideration.
Certification is done by the Florida Department of Management Services. You have to be certified before the preference applies, so do it before you bid.
records.agency: Florida Department of Management Services

records.title: Veterans preference in state and local government hiring and retention
records.summary: Florida and its counties, cities, and districts must give preference in appointment and retention to Veterans and certain family members. Reserve and Guard members and honorably discharged Veterans are also included.
eligibility: Disabled Veterans who served on active duty, received an honorable discharge, and have established a present service-connected disability, or who receive VA compensation
The spouse of a person with a total service-connected disability, or the spouse of a person missing in action
A parent or the widow or widower of a servicemember who died in combat-related circumstances
A Veteran who served at least 1 day during a wartime period as defined in Fla. Stat. 1.01(14), not counting active duty for training
Any Veteran as defined in the statute, not counting active duty for training
A current member of any reserve component of the U.S. Armed Forces or the Florida National Guard
details: Employers may waive a postsecondary education requirement for reserve and Guard members and for honorably discharged Veterans who are otherwise qualified.
How the preference is applied depends on the hiring process. Fla. Stat. 295.08 covers positions using a numerically based selection process and 295.085 covers positions that do not.
Fla. Stat. 295.09 covers reinstatement, reemployment, and promotion preference. Fla. Stat. 295.11 gives you an investigation and administrative hearing route if a preferred applicant is not hired.
State agencies and political subdivisions must develop written Veteran recruitment plans with annual hiring goals and must track preference usage statistically.
A separate section, Fla. Stat. 295.188, addresses preference in hiring Veterans by private employers.
records.agency: Florida Department of Veterans' Affairs and Florida Department of Management Services

records.title: Disabled Veteran homestead tax exemption
records.summary: Georgia gives qualifying disabled Veterans a large homestead exemption on the home they own and live in. The exemption amount is set by a federal index and changes from year to year, so confirm the current figure with your county tax commissioner.
records.amount: Up to $126,526 of assessed value for FY2026
eligibility: You are an honorably discharged Georgia Veteran
You own the home and use it as your primary residence
You are rated 100 percent service-connected disabled by the VA, or rated below 100 percent but entitled to compensation at the 100 percent rate because of unemployability
You may also qualify through a statutory award for loss or permanent loss of use of feet or hands, loss of sight, or permanent eye impairment
An unremarried surviving spouse or minor child of a qualified deceased Veteran may continue the exemption while occupying the home as a residence
details: The maximum is not a Georgia number. O.C.G.A. 48-5-48 ties it to the federal Specially Adapted Housing grant amount under 38 U.S.C. 2102, which the Secretary of Veterans Affairs raises each year by a cost-of-construction index.
For fiscal year 2026 that amount is $126,526, effective 1 October 2025, a 3.87 percent increase on the previous year. Confirmed against the Federal Register notice, not a secondary summary.

IMPORTANT: the Georgia Department of Veterans Service page still publishes the 2025 figure of $121,812. That is the previous year. If a county quotes you the lower number, the federal index is the authority and it is worth asking.
Claimed through your county tax commissioner, not the state. Counties set their own filing deadlines.
records.agency: Georgia Department of Veterans Service and county tax commissioners

records.title: Georgia HERO Scholarship for Guard and Reserve members and their families
records.summary: The HERO Scholarship helps pay for college for Georgia National Guard and U.S. Military Reserve members who served in a combat zone, and for the children and spouses of those members. It is administered by the Georgia Student Finance Commission.
records.amount: Up to $2,000 per academic school year, prorated below 12 credit hours, up to $8,000 total for the equivalent of four academic years. Funding is subject to legislative appropriation and awards are first come, first served.
eligibility: Category 1: an active member of the Georgia National Guard or U.S. Military Reserves deployed to a combat zone on or after February 1, 2003, for at least 181 cumulative days, or evacuated because of severe injuries
Category 2: a child of a member who meets the Category 1 service, born before or within nine months of the start of the qualifying service, and age 25 or younger during that service
Category 3: a child of a member who was killed in the combat zone, or who died or became 100 percent disabled from injuries received there, with the same birth and age conditions
Category 4: the spouse of a former member who was killed in a designated combat zone, or who died or became 100 percent disabled from injuries received there, on or after February 1, 2003
You must meet U.S. citizenship or eligible non-citizen requirements
You must have lived in Georgia for 12 consecutive months before enrollment
You must attend an eligible University System of Georgia, Technical College System of Georgia, or eligible Georgia private non-profit college or university
You must comply with Georgia's drug-free postsecondary education law, and register with Selective Service if that applies to you
details: There is a filing deadline tied to the date the service member returned from the combat zone, and eligibility ends a set number of years after that date. The exact windows are on the program's application procedure and deadline page, so check them before you assume you still qualify.
Category 2 awards are counted per qualifying term of service, up to four qualifying terms, and still cannot exceed the overall total.
records.agency: Georgia Student Finance Commission

records.title: Georgia income tax exclusion for military retirement income
records.summary: Georgia lets military retirees exclude part of their retirement income from state income tax. How much you can exclude depends on your age, and younger retirees can exclude an extra amount if they also have earned income.
records.amount: Georgia Department of Veterans Service lists: under age 62, up to $17,500 of military retirement income, plus an additional $17,500 if you have at least $17,500 in earned income. Ages 62 to 64, up to $35,000 under Georgia's general retirement income exclusion. Age 65 and over, up to $65,000.
eligibility: You retired from military service and receive military retirement income
You file a Georgia income tax return
The additional exclusion for retirees under age 62 depends on earned income. The two state agencies word the test slightly differently, so see the details
The general retirement income exclusion is open to anyone 62 or older, and also to anyone permanently and totally disabled regardless of age
details: Two state agencies describe the under-62 rule in slightly different words, and the difference could matter to you. The Department of Veterans Service says an additional exemption of up to $17,500 is available for Veterans under 62 who have "at least $17,500 of earned income". The Department of Revenue says the additional $17,500 is for "taxpayers with more than $17,500 of earned income in Georgia". Revenue is the tax authority, and its version adds a Georgia-source requirement and reads as a strict threshold. If your earned income is close to $17,500, ask Revenue before you file.
The military-specific exclusion for retirees under 62 began 1 January 2022.
The amounts for ages 62 and over come from Georgia's general retirement income exclusion, which is not limited to Veterans. Military retirement income counts toward it.

If you are permanently and totally disabled you can take the general retirement income exclusion at any age, without waiting until 62. Revenue states this plainly, and a disabled Veteran under 62 is exactly the person likely to miss it.

The Department of Revenue does not publish the age-based dollar figures on its retirement income exclusion page. It points to the Individual Income Tax Instruction Booklet, Form IT-511, for the filing year. That booklet is the figure to trust, since the exclusion has been amended by the legislature more than once.
The exclusion is claimed on your Georgia return. There is no separate application.
records.agency: Georgia Department of Revenue

records.title: Veterans preference points for State of Georgia employment
records.summary: Georgia adds preference credits to the applications of qualifying Veterans applying for state jobs. Wartime and conflict-period service earns a 5-point credit, and service-connected disability or certain survivor status earns a 10-point credit.
records.amount: A 5-point credit for qualifying conflict-period service. A 10-point credit for the disability and survivor categories.
eligibility: 5-point credit: you served on active duty in the U.S. Armed Forces during a period of armed conflict, or served as a National Guard or Reserve member on active duty during a qualifying operation
10-point credit: you have a VA service-connected disability rating of 10 percent or more
10-point credit: you are over 55 and receive a disability pension or compensation
10-point credit: you are the spouse of a disabled Veteran who is disqualified from employment
10-point credit: you are the unmarried widow or widower of a deceased Veteran
details: You claim the credit on the State of Georgia employment application and support it with documentation such as a DD Form 214 or verification of your service-connected disability status.
This is a Georgia state hiring preference. Federal hiring preference is a separate program under 5 U.S.C. 2108, and local governments set their own rules.
records.agency: State of Georgia hiring agencies, with guidance from the Georgia Department of Veterans Service

records.title: Free Georgia Veteran driver's license and ID card
records.summary: Georgia issues a driver's license and ID card marked with a U.S. flag and the word VETERAN at no cost to qualifying Veterans. You apply in person at any Department of Driver Services office.
records.amount: No cost for the Veteran driver's license. Georgia DDS states that qualifying Veterans and service members may obtain a Veteran license or ID at reduced or no cost.
eligibility: You are a current Georgia resident
You were discharged from military service under honorable conditions, or received a medical discharge
Georgia National Guard members qualify through active duty service or 20 years of service
An honorary Veteran license or ID is available to the spouse of a deceased Veteran, or to the spouse of a disabled Veteran who does not drive
details: Bring the Member 4 copy of your DD Form 214, proof of residency, a birth certificate or passport, your Social Security card, two documents showing your residential address, and name change documentation if it applies.
A DDS representative gives a vision exam, verifies eligibility, and issues the license.
If you need a replacement DD Form 214, the National Archives can supply additional copies.
records.agency: Georgia Department of Driver Services

records.title: Free and discounted hunting and fishing licenses for Veterans
records.summary: Georgia gives returning Veterans a one-time free hunting and fishing license, and offers discounted lifetime and disability licenses to other qualifying Veterans. The Wildlife Resources Division of the Department of Natural Resources runs the program.
eligibility: Georgia residency is required for all of these license types
One-time free license: you served at least 90 days on active federal duty and were honorably discharged on or after July 1, 2005
Discounted lifetime licenses: you were discharged under honorable conditions
Disability licenses: you have a permanent and total disability rating from the VA or another government agency
A free lifetime honorary fishing license is available to totally blind residents
details: The one-time returning Veteran license is free and valid for one year. It is a one-time benefit, not an annual one.

Lifetime sportsman's licenses are sold at reduced rates, and the reduction changes with the age band you fall into. Multi-year disability licenses are offered as an alternative to annual renewals. Ask the Wildlife Resources Division for the current price for your situation rather than assuming a figure.
Contact the Wildlife Resources Division at 800-366-2661 or through georgiawildlife.com to buy a license or confirm eligibility.
records.agency: Georgia Department of Natural Resources, Wildlife Resources Division

records.title: Free Veteran and military license plates
records.summary: Georgia offers several Veteran and military specialty license plates with no registration, manufacturing, or annual fee on the first plate. You apply through your county tax office using Form MV-9W.
records.amount: No registration fee, manufacturing fee, or annual fee for one of these specialty plates. A second plate costs $25 manufacturing plus the annual renewal fees.
eligibility: Most of these plates are available to Georgia Veterans discharged under honorable conditions
Active duty service members who are Georgia residents also qualify
An unremarried surviving spouse of a qualified deceased Veteran may qualify
Some plates have their own conditions, such as proof of a specific medal award or of service in a specific conflict
details: Plate categories include the Veteran's plate, the Woman Veteran's plate, the Retired Military plate, commemorative service plates for specific conflicts, military medal award plates, and reserve component plates. Georgia also issues disabled Veteran, Purple Heart, Medal of Honor, former prisoner of war, Pearl Harbor survivor, and Gold Star plates under separate code sections.
Submit a completed Form MV-9W with a copy of your DD Form 214 to your county tax office. The form comes from the Georgia Department of Revenue Motor Vehicle Division.
records.agency: Georgia Department of Revenue, Motor Vehicle Division, through county tag offices
records.statuteRef: O.C.G.A. 40-2-85.1 and related sections in O.C.G.A. Title 40, Chapter 2

records.title: Veterans Business Certificate of Exemption from local business fees
records.summary: A qualifying disabled Veteran can get a certificate that exempts them for ten years from local occupation taxes and business and regulatory fees for peddling, running a business, or practicing a profession. You apply through your county probate court.
records.amount: Exempts you from any occupation tax, administrative fee, or regulatory fee imposed by local governments for a period of ten years.
eligibility: You were discharged under honorable conditions
You have a service-connected disability rating of 10 percent or more
details: Complete VS Form 40-025, the Application for a Veterans Business Certificate of Exemption. Take it with an ID card, your DD Form 214, and your VA Summary of Benefits letter to your county probate court.
The clerk of the probate court provides a notarized letter or affidavit from the judge, which you then use to register your business with your county tax commissioner.

Some counties also ask for Form 40-026, the Veteran's Certificate of State License and Tax Exemption. A Georgia Department of Veterans Service field office can help if your county's requirements differ.
This exemption covers local government fees. It does not exempt you from state or federal taxes.
records.agency: Georgia Department of Veterans Service, with county probate courts and county tax commissioners

records.title: Burial in a Georgia Veterans Memorial Cemetery
records.summary: Georgia operates two state Veterans memorial cemeteries, at Glennville and at Milledgeville. There is no cost for the gravesite, vault, marker, use of the committal chapel, or the burial itself.
records.amount: No burial fees. There is no cost for the gravesite, vault, marker, use of the committal chapel, and burial.
eligibility: Veterans who meet VA standards for burial
Retired Reserve and National Guard members, and those with a service-connected rating
Active duty service members who die in service
Spouses of Veterans
Minor children of Veterans
Adult unmarried disabled children of Veterans
details: Contact the cemetery directly to schedule a burial and to submit documentation. Depending on the relationship, that can include the DD Form 214 or other discharge papers, a marriage certificate, a birth certificate, or medical records.
Each cemetery has a welcome center, a committal chapel, in-ground interment areas, and columbaria for cremated remains.
Cemetery offices are open 8 a.m. to 4:30 p.m., Monday through Friday, except state holidays. Grounds are open for visitation from 8 a.m. to dusk daily.
records.agency: Georgia Department of Veterans Service

records.title: Georgia War Veterans Homes skilled nursing care
records.summary: Georgia runs two state Veterans homes providing skilled nursing care, one in Augusta and one in Milledgeville. A nominal daily fee applies, and the VA pays the daily fee in full for Veterans who meet certain service-connected criteria.
records.amount: A nominal daily fee is charged. The Georgia Department of Veterans Service states that Veterans meeting certain service-connected criteria have their daily fees paid in full by VA. Ask the admissions office for the current daily rate.
eligibility: You are an aged or infirm Georgia war Veteran needing skilled nursing care
Veterans with a service-connected disability rating of 70 percent or higher receive special consideration
Admission criteria are set by the homes, so review the eligibility requirements and speak with an admissions office before applying
details: The Georgia War Veterans Home at Milledgeville is a 248-bed facility on about 17 acres, licensed and certified by the U.S. Department of Veterans Affairs. It provides skilled nursing care, specialty care for residents with Alzheimer's, a sub-acute rehabilitation unit, and a transitional support unit that opened in September 2025 offering mental and behavioral health services alongside skilled nursing.
The Georgia War Veterans Nursing Home at Augusta sits next to the Augusta University campus, across from the Charlie Norwood VA Medical Center.

Applications start at georgiawarveteranshome.com. The Augusta location asks that you schedule a visit with the Admissions Office in advance. Milledgeville admissions hours are 8 a.m. to 3 p.m., Monday through Friday, and its admissions number is 478-445-4295.
Eligible Veterans may be able to use federal VA Aid and Attendance benefits to help cover the cost.
records.agency: Georgia Department of Veterans Service

records.title: Resident Disabled Veteran Lifetime Sportsman License
records.summary: A North Carolina resident Veteran rated 50 percent or more disabled by the VA can buy a lifetime hunting and fishing sportsman license for a one-time fee of $100. It is good for the rest of your life.
records.amount: $100.00 one time, for a lifetime license
eligibility: You are a resident of North Carolina
You are a 50 percent or more disabled Veteran as determined by the United States Department of Veterans Affairs
details: The license covers taking wild animals and birds by lawful methods other than trapping during open seasons, plus hook-and-line fishing in inland waters and public mountain trout waters.

The statute also creates a Resident Totally Disabled Lifetime Sportsman License at the same $100 fee for a resident who is totally and permanently disabled as determined by the Social Security Administration.
These are inland privileges. Coastal recreational fishing is licensed separately.
records.agency: North Carolina Wildlife Resources Commission

records.title: Disabled Veteran property tax homestead exclusion
records.summary: North Carolina excludes the first $45,000 of appraised value of your permanent residence from property tax if you are a Veteran with a VA certified permanent and total service-connected disability. An unremarried surviving spouse can qualify too.
records.amount: The first $45,000 of appraised value of the residence is excluded from taxation
eligibility: Your character of service at separation was honorable or under honorable conditions
And the VA or another federal agency has certified that, as of January 1 before the tax year, you have a service-connected, permanent, and total disability
Or you had received benefits under 38 U.S.C. 2101 as of that January 1
Or the Veteran is deceased and the VA certified that the death resulted from a service-connected condition
You are a North Carolina resident and an owner of the permanent residence
An unremarried surviving spouse of a disabled Veteran also counts as a qualifying owner
There is no income limit written into this particular exclusion
details: The statute directs you to file during the regular listing period, but applications must be accepted at any time up to and through June 1 preceding the tax year for which the exclusion is claimed. Do not wait past June 1.
You apply through your county tax office, not the state. Counties administer the listing period and process the paperwork.
You have to submit either a copy of the Veteran's disability certification or evidence of the benefits received under 38 U.S.C. 2101.
A married couple who own and occupy the home together get the full exclusion even if only one of them qualifies.

You do not lose the exclusion by being away temporarily for health reasons, or by an extended stay in a rest home or nursing home, so long as the residence is empty or lived in by your spouse or another dependent.
Co-owners who are not married to each other each have to apply separately. Each qualifying co-owner gets the full exclusion, capped at their proportionate share of the property's value.
A qualifying owner receiving this exclusion cannot also receive the other property tax relief programs in Chapter 105, so compare before you choose.
records.agency: North Carolina Department of Revenue, administered by county tax offices

records.title: In-state tuition rate for Veterans and their dependents
records.summary: A Veteran using federal education benefits can pay the North Carolina in-state tuition rate at a public college without waiting out the usual 12 month residency period, as long as North Carolina is their home and they file a letter of intent to establish residence.
eligibility: You completed active duty of not less than 90 days in the Armed Forces, the US Public Health Service, or NOAA, and were discharged or released from that service
You qualify as a covered individual under 38 U.S.C. 3679(c), which also reaches certain dependents using transferred benefits
Your abode is in North Carolina
You give the institution a letter of intent to establish residence in North Carolina
details: This route skips the standard 12 month durational residency requirement that other students must meet.
The statute puts the burden of proof on the person applying, so bring your DD-214 and your VA certificate of eligibility to the residency determination.

A separate statute, N.C.G.S. 116-143.3, gives the in-state rate to active duty members stationed in North Carolina and their spouses and dependent children, and lets them keep it if they stay continuously enrolled after a reassignment, a retirement, or an honorable discharge followed by establishing residency within 30 days.
records.agency: University of North Carolina System and the North Carolina Community College System

records.title: Deduction for military retirement pay and Survivor Benefit Plan payments
records.summary: North Carolina lets you deduct military retirement pay from your state taxable income if you served at least 20 years or were medically retired. Survivor Benefit Plan payments to a beneficiary of an eligible retiree are deductible too.
eligibility: You receive retirement pay from the United States government for service in the uniformed services
The statute uses the definition of uniformed services in 10 U.S.C. 101(a)(5), which reaches beyond the Armed Forces to the commissioned corps of the Public Health Service and of NOAA
And you served at least 20 years in the uniformed services, or you were medically retired under 10 U.S.C. Chapter 61
Severance pay for separation under 10 U.S.C. Chapter 61 does not qualify
A beneficiary receiving payments from a plan defined in 10 U.S.C. 1447, the Survivor Benefit Plan, can deduct them if the retired member met the conditions above
The deduction is only allowed to the extent the payments are included in your adjusted gross income
details: This deduction applies to taxable years beginning on or after 1 January 2022.
There is no cap. North Carolina deducts the whole qualifying amount, which is a meaningfully better deal than the capped subtractions in states like Virginia and California.
The 20 year threshold is the catch. A retiree with 19 years and a non-medical separation does not qualify at all, and there is no partial deduction.

This is separate from the older Bailey settlement deduction under G.S. 105-153.5(b)(5) for certain federal, state, and local retirement benefits. The statute says the same amount cannot be deducted under both, so if you are a Bailey-protected retiree, work out which one applies before filing.
The deduction is claimed on your North Carolina return. It is not automatic.
records.agency: North Carolina Department of Revenue
records.amount: The full amount of qualifying retirement pay. The statute sets no dollar cap.

records.title: Military and Veteran license plates with no additional plate fee
records.summary: North Carolina issues a long list of military and Veteran special registration plates, and the fee table sets the additional special plate charge for them at none. You still pay the ordinary registration fee.
records.amount: No additional special plate fee beyond the regular registration fee
eligibility: 100% Disabled Veteran plate: issuable to a Veteran of the Armed Forces who suffered a 100 percent service-connected disability
Partially Disabled Veteran plate: issuable to a Veteran who suffered a service-connected disability of less than 100 percent
Military Veteran plate: issuable to an individual who served honorably in the Armed Forces, and it shows the branch insignia
Purple Heart Recipient plate: issuable to a recipient of the Purple Heart award
Prisoner of War plate: issuable to a member or Veteran member of the Armed Forces who was captured and held prisoner by forces hostile to the United States while serving
details: The statutory fee table lists an additional fee of none for Active Member of the National Guard, Bronze Star Recipient, Bronze Star Combat Recipient, 100% Disabled Veteran, Ex-Prisoner of War, Gold Star Lapel Button, Legion of Merit, Legion of Valor, Military Veteran, Military Wartime Veteran, Partially Disabled Veteran, Pearl Harbor Survivor, Purple Heart Recipient, and Silver Star Recipient.
The disabled Veteran and Purple Heart plates are available for motorcycles as well as motor vehicles.
The plate statutes do not by themselves grant a disabled parking placard or waive the regular registration fee. Ask NC DMV about those separately.
records.agency: North Carolina Division of Motor Vehicles

records.title: North Carolina Scholarship for Children of Wartime Veterans
records.summary: North Carolina awards scholarships to the children of Veterans who were killed, disabled, held as prisoners of war, or listed missing in action. The award is worth eight academic semesters, and you have eight years to use them.
records.amount: Eight academic semesters, usable within eight years
eligibility: You are under 25 years of age at the time you apply
You are a resident of and domiciled in North Carolina
Your Veteran parent was a legal resident of North Carolina when entering the qualifying period of military service, or you were born in North Carolina and have lived here continuously since birth
You meet the definition of child in 37 U.S.C. 401

Your Veteran parent falls into one of the statutory classes: killed in action or died of service-connected injuries, rated 100 percent for a wartime service-connected disability, rated 20 percent or more but less than 100 percent or awarded a Purple Heart for combat wounds, deceased or drawing a nonservice-connected permanent and total disability pension after combat zone or campaign service, or listed as missing in action, captured in the line of duty, or forcibly detained or interned
details: The statute sorts awards into Class I-A, I-B, II, III, and IV. Class II and Class III are each capped at 100 children per year. The other classes are not capped in the statute.

At a North Carolina public institution the program pays the allocable costs for room, board, tuition, and other charges. At a private institution it instead pays a fixed monetary allowance per academic term, set by the Director of the Budget, with a lower uniform rate for Class I-B than for the other classes. Confirm the current allowance figures with the agency before you rely on them.

The state portal lists a February 14 deadline for the classes covering Veterans rated less than 100 percent disabled or who served in a combat zone. Other classes have separate deadlines. Confirm the exact date for your class on the portal each year, because the portal closes once a term's deadline passes.
