details: The exemption covers tuition, dues, fees, and other required charges, including correspondence course fees. It specifically excludes general deposit fees, student services fees, and any charge for lodging, board, or clothing.
The cap is a cumulative 150 credit hours across all use of this exemption, not 150 hours per institution or per degree.
Related provisions in the same chapter extend the benefit to some spouses and children. Ask the institution's veteran services office about Hazlewood Legacy.
Apply through the financial aid or veteran services office at the Texas public institution you attend.
records.agency: Texas public institutions of higher education

records.title: Military employment preference for state agency jobs
records.summary: Texas state agencies must give hiring preference to Veterans and certain military family members over other applicants who are not better qualified, and every agency has a goal of Veterans making up at least 20 percent of its workforce.
records.amount: Hiring preference, plus a 20 percent Veteran workforce goal at every state agency
eligibility: A Veteran, including a Veteran with a disability
A Veteran's surviving spouse who has not remarried
An orphan of a Veteran killed while on active duty
The spouse of a member of the US armed forces or Texas National Guard serving on active duty

The spouse of a Veteran, where the spouse is the household's primary income and the Veteran has a total disability rating based on a service-connected disability of at least 70 percent or individual unemployability
details: The preference applies over other applicants for the same position who do not have a greater qualification. It is a tie-breaker in your favour, not an automatic hire.
The statute sets an order of priority: a Veteran with a disability first, then a Veteran, then a qualifying spouse, then a Veteran's surviving spouse.
Each state agency must set a goal of hiring Veterans into full-time positions equal to at least 20 percent of its total employees, and may set a higher goal.
records.agency: Texas state agencies

records.title: Dependency and Indemnity Compensation (DIC) for survivors
records.summary: A tax-free monthly payment to the surviving spouse, children, or dependent parents of a service member who died on duty, or of a Veteran who died from a service-connected condition.
records.amount: Tax-free monthly payment, varying by survivor type and dependents
eligibility: The service member died while on active duty, active duty for training, or inactive-duty training
Or the Veteran died from a service-connected condition
Or the Veteran had a totally disabling service-connected rating for 10 years before death, 5 years after discharge, or 1 year if a former prisoner of war
Surviving spouse: married within 15 years of discharge, or married at least a year, or you had a child together
Surviving children: unmarried, under 18, or under 23 and in school, and not already covered by the spouse payment
Surviving parents: biological, adoptive, or foster, with income below the limit
details: REMARRIAGE RULE, which catches many families out: a surviving spouse who remarries can keep DIC if they were at least 57 at remarriage before December 2003, or at least 55 at remarriage from January 2021 onward.
Rates change every year with a cost-of-living adjustment, so check the current table rather than a figure you were quoted before.
Filing is free. An accredited service officer will help at no charge.
records.agency: US Department of Veterans Affairs

records.title: Survivors and Dependents Educational Assistance (Chapter 35)
records.summary: Monthly payments toward education for the children and spouses of a Veteran who is permanently and totally disabled from service, died from a service-connected cause, or is missing, captured, or detained.
records.amount: Up to 36 months of monthly payments, or 45 months if training began before August 2018
eligibility: The Veteran or service member is permanently and totally disabled from a service-connected condition, died of a service-connected cause, is missing in action, captured, forcibly detained, or hospitalized for a service-connected disability
Children: any age if eligibility began on or after 1 August 2023. Otherwise 18, or younger with a high school diploma or GED
Spouses: eligible whether married or unmarried at the time of application
details: TIME LIMITS depend on when eligibility began. For children eligible on or after 1 August 2023 there is no time limit at all. Before that date it is generally 8 years, ending at age 26.
For spouses, no limit if the qualifying event was on or after 1 August 2023. Before that, generally 10 years, or 20 years if the service member died on active duty.
This is separate from the Post-9/11 GI Bill and from transferred GI Bill entitlement. Compare them before choosing, because you may be eligible for more than one.
records.agency: US Department of Veterans Affairs

records.title: Specially Adapted Housing and Special Home Adaptation grants
records.summary: Grant money to buy, build, or modify a home so you can live in it with a service-connected disability. You can draw on the grant up to six separate times over your lifetime.
records.amount: Up to $126,526 (SAH) or $25,349 (SHA) in FY2026, usable across 6 lifetime uses
eligibility: You own or will own the home
SAH: qualifying service-connected disabilities include the loss, or loss of use, of more than one limb, and blindness in both eyes within set limits
SHA: qualifying disabilities include the loss, or loss of use, of both hands, and severe burn or respiratory injuries
details: Both grants cover buying, building, or adapting a permanent home to suit the disability.

FY2026 maximums, effective 1 October 2025: $126,526 for a Specially Adapted Housing grant under 38 U.S.C. 2101(a), and $25,349 for a Special Home Adaptation grant under 2101(b). Both rose 3.87 percent on the year.
Temporary Residence Adaptation, for adapting a home you are living in temporarily, is capped separately at $50,961 under 2101(a) or $9,099 under 2101(b) for FY2026.
You do not have to spend it all at once. You can use part in one year and the remainder later, up to six uses in total.
These figures change every 1 October with the cost-of-construction index, so check the current year before you plan around them.
records.agency: US Department of Veterans Affairs

records.title: Burial in a VA national cemetery
records.summary: Veterans, and in many cases their spouses and dependent children, can be buried in a VA national cemetery. Spouses remain eligible even if they remarried.
eligibility: Veterans who did not separate under dishonorable conditions
Service members who die while on active duty
Surviving spouses of Veterans, including those who have since remarried
Minor children, and unmarried adult dependent children, of Veterans
Special rules cover Reserve members, ROTC officers, NOAA and Public Health Service officers, WWII Merchant Mariners, Philippine Armed Forces Veterans, and Hmong Veterans
details: That surviving spouses stay eligible after remarrying surprises a lot of families, and it is worth knowing before making other arrangements.
Plan ahead. You can apply for a pre-need eligibility determination so your family is not making this decision under pressure.
Many states also run their own Veteran cemeteries with separate rules. Check your state page as well as this.
records.agency: US Department of Veterans Affairs, National Cemetery Administration

records.title: Post-9/11 GI Bill
records.summary: Pays the full cost of in-state tuition and fees at a public college, plus a monthly housing allowance and a books stipend. Up to 36 months of benefits, and for most Veterans it never expires.
records.amount: Up to 36 months. Full in-state public tuition and fees, plus housing and books.
eligibility: At least 90 days on active duty on or after 11 September 2001
Or you received a Purple Heart on or after that date and were honorably discharged
Or you served 30 continuous days and were discharged for a service-connected disability
Or you are a dependent using benefits transferred to you
details: Maximum entitlement is 36 months. Serving 56 months or more can open access to up to 48 months across combined programs.

IMPORTANT DEADLINE: if you were discharged before 1 January 2013, benefits expire 15 years after you separated. Discharged on or after that date, there is no expiration, thanks to the Forever GI Bill.
Full in-state tuition and fees at public schools. Private and foreign schools are capped at a set rate.
The monthly housing allowance is based on the cost of living where your school is located, and is not paid during school breaks.
It also funds tutoring, licensing and certification tests, and work-study.
records.agency: US Department of Veterans Affairs

records.title: Veteran-owned small business certification (VetCert)
records.summary: Certifying your business as Veteran-owned, or service-disabled Veteran-owned, lets you compete for federal contracts set aside specifically for you. The government targets at least 5 percent of federal contracting dollars at service-disabled Veteran-owned firms.
records.amount: Access to sole-source and set-aside federal contracts
eligibility: The VA identifies you as a Veteran, or as a service-disabled Veteran for SDVOSB status
At least 51 percent of the business is owned and controlled by one or more Veterans
For SDVOSB, at least 51 percent is owned by service-disabled Veterans
The business meets SBA small business size standards for its industry
A permanently disabled Veteran may still qualify where a spouse or caregiver runs daily operations
details: Certification is handled by the Small Business Administration. Apply through the SBA certifications portal, not through the VA.
Certified Veteran-owned firms can compete under the VA Vets First program as well as government-wide set-asides.
The SBA also runs a Surplus Personal Property program giving access to unused federal property through State Agencies for Surplus Property.
Help line: 866-722-4357, Monday to Friday, 8am to 6pm Eastern.
records.agency: US Small Business Administration

records.title: VA disability compensation
records.summary: A tax-free monthly payment for an illness or injury caused or made worse by your military service. This is the benefit most other VA benefits key off, so it is usually the first thing to file for.
records.amount: Tax-free monthly payment, scaled to your disability rating
eligibility: You have a current illness or injury affecting your body or mind
And you served on active duty, active duty for training, or inactive duty training
And at least one applies: the condition began during service, service made a pre-existing condition worse, or a service-related disability appeared after discharge
An other than honorable, bad conduct, or dishonorable discharge may block eligibility, but a discharge upgrade or a VA Character of Discharge review can change that
details: Presumptive conditions are approved without you having to prove service caused them. These include a chronic illness appearing within one year of discharge, illnesses linked to toxic exposure, and conditions resulting from being a prisoner of war.
Covered conditions include chronic back pain, lung disease, hearing loss, PTSD, depression, and cancers linked to toxic exposure.
Rates change annually with a cost-of-living adjustment, so check the current rate table rather than relying on a figure you were quoted before.
Filing is free. An accredited Veterans Service Officer will help you file at no charge, and you should never pay a percentage of your back pay to anyone.
records.agency: US Department of Veterans Affairs

records.title: VA health care
records.summary: Enrolling in VA health care gives you access to VA medical centers and clinics nationwide. The PACT Act widened eligibility considerably, so it is worth re-checking even if you were turned down before.
eligibility: If you enlisted after 7 September 1980, or entered active duty after 16 October 1981, you generally need 24 continuous months of service or the full period you were called up
That requirement is waived if you were discharged for a service-connected disability, for a hardship, or under an early out
Reserve and National Guard members must have completed their full federal active-duty period
You must not have a dishonorable discharge. Other than honorable and bad conduct discharges may still qualify after a discharge upgrade or a Character of Discharge review
details: VA sorts enrollees into one of eight priority groups. Your group affects how quickly you enrol and what copays you pay.

You land in a higher priority group if you have a service-connected disability, are a post-9/11 combat Veteran, were a prisoner of war, hold a Purple Heart, or were exposed to toxins such as Agent Orange or asbestos.
The PACT Act extended eligibility to Veterans who served in Vietnam, the Gulf War, Iraq, Afghanistan, or any other combat zone after 9/11. If you were previously denied, apply again.
records.agency: US Department of Veterans Affairs

records.title: VA-backed home loan
records.summary: A VA guaranty lets a lender offer better terms than a conventional mortgage. Nearly 90 percent of VA-backed loans are made with no down payment at all.
records.amount: Nearly 90 percent of VA-backed loans are made with no down payment
eligibility: Veterans, service members, and some surviving spouses qualify based on service history and duty status
You need a Certificate of Eligibility to prove to a lender that you qualify
You still have to meet the lender's own credit and income requirements: the VA guarantees part of the loan, it does not lend the money
details: Four programs: purchase loans, Native American Direct Loans, interest rate reduction refinance loans, and cash-out refinance loans.
A VA funding fee usually applies, and some Veterans are exempt from it, including many with a service-connected disability. Ask before you assume you owe it.
The benefit is reusable. Using it once does not spend it forever.
Be cautious of refinance offers that arrive by mail or phone shortly after you close. Aggressive VA loan churning is a well-documented problem and it costs Veterans money.
records.agency: US Department of Veterans Affairs

records.title: Veteran Readiness and Employment (Chapter 31)
records.summary: If a service-connected disability limits your ability to work, VR&E helps you retrain, find work, or start a business. It is separate from the GI Bill and does not use up your GI Bill entitlement.
eligibility: You have a service-connected disability that limits your ability to work or prevents you from working
Eligibility is decided case by case with a Vocational Rehabilitation Counselor
details: Five tracks: returning to a former job, rapid access to employment, self-employment, long-term training services, and independent living for Veterans not currently able to work.
It also provides educational and career counselling.
Worth comparing against the GI Bill before you choose. VR&E is aimed at Veterans whose disability affects their capacity to work, and the two programs are separate entitlements.
records.agency: US Department of Veterans Affairs

records.title: Free help filing your federal VA disability claim
records.summary: The Virginia Department of Veterans Services is responsible by statute for benefits claims processing for Virginia-domiciled Veterans and their eligible spouses, orphans, and dependents. Its benefits staff help you prepare and file federal VA claims.
eligibility: Virginia-domiciled Veterans of the Armed Forces of the United States
Eligible spouses, orphans, and dependents of those Veterans
The Department sets the detailed eligibility guidelines, which must meet the intent of the federal statutes and regulations for the programs involved
details: This is Virginia state help with a federal benefit. The claim itself goes to the U.S. Department of Veterans Affairs. The state staff who help you prepare it work for the Commonwealth and do not charge you.
The statute also directs the Department to build an automated system for electronic preparation of Veterans disability claims, so it can move claims faster.

The Department must cooperate with the U.S. Department of Veterans Affairs, the U.S. Department of Housing and Urban Development, and the U.S. Department of Labor on Veterans benefits and services, under Va. Code 2.2-2004.
Never pay a fee to have an initial VA disability claim prepared. Accredited representatives and state service officers do it at no cost.
records.agency: Virginia Department of Veterans Services

records.title: DV license plates and no annual registration fee on one vehicle
records.summary: Virginia issues red, white, and blue DV plates to any Veteran the VA certifies has a service-connected disability. One vehicle you own and use personally is exempt from the annual registration fee.
records.amount: No annual registration fee under Va. Code 46.2-694, and no annual fee under 46.2-725 B 3, on one motor vehicle
eligibility: The U.S. Department of Veterans Affairs has certified that you have a service-connected disability
Your application must include that certification from the VA
The fee exemption covers one motor vehicle owned and used personally by the disabled Veteran
An unremarried surviving spouse of a disabled Veteran may also be issued the plates, and a DV plate may transfer to the unremarried surviving spouse on the Veteran's death
details: Standard DV plates do not by themselves authorize you to park in spaces reserved for people with disabilities that limit or impair the ability to walk.

If you also have a disability that limits or impairs your ability to walk, you can apply for DV disabled parking plates showing the international symbol of access. Those do authorize accessible parking. That application needs a signed certification from a licensed physician, podiatrist, chiropractor, advanced practice registered nurse, or physician assistant.
The registration fee exemption is available whether you display the DV plates or the standard passenger plates, as long as you have filed the service-connected disability certification.
Handled through the Virginia Department of Motor Vehicles.
records.agency: Virginia Department of Motor Vehicles

records.title: Lifetime hunting and freshwater fishing license for disabled Veterans
records.summary: A resident Veteran with a service-connected disability can buy a nontransferable license valid for life to hunt and freshwater fish anywhere in Virginia. It is free at a total and permanent rating and discounted at lower ratings.
records.amount: No cost at totally and permanently disabled. $50 at 70 percent or more. $75 at 50 percent or more. $100 at 30 percent or more.
eligibility: You are a resident Veteran disabled due to a service-connected disability
Rated totally and permanently disabled by the U.S. Department of Veterans Affairs: no cost
Rated 70 percent or more but less than totally and permanently disabled: $50
Rated 50 percent or more but less than 70 percent: $75
Rated 30 percent or more but less than 50 percent: $100
details: The license is valid for life and is nontransferable.
You can buy it as a combined hunt and freshwater fish license, or hunt only, or freshwater fish only. The price depends on which one you buy.
One limit worth knowing: the license does not let you fish in waters stocked with trout by the Department or another public body. You need the separate trout license for those.
Issued by the Virginia Department of Wildlife Resources under 4VAC15-20-65.
records.agency: Virginia Department of Wildlife Resources

records.title: Full real property tax exemption at a 100 percent permanent and total rating
records.summary: If the VA rates you 100 percent service-connected, permanent and total, Virginia exempts your principal residence from local real property tax. The exemption covers the dwelling plus up to one acre of land it sits on.
records.amount: The full assessed value of the qualifying dwelling plus up to one acre of land. The statute sets no dollar cap.
eligibility: The U.S. Department of Veterans Affairs has rated you 100 percent service-connected, permanent, and total
You occupy the real property as your principal place of residence
Applies to tax years beginning on or after January 1, 2011
A surviving spouse also qualifies if the Veteran died on or after January 1, 2011 and the spouse has not remarried
A surviving spouse may move to a different principal residence and keep the exemption
details: The exemption starts on the date of your rating if you already own a qualifying home, or on the date you acquire the property if you buy after January 1, 2011.

You claim it by filing an affidavit or written statement with your county, city, or town under Va. Code 58.1-3219.6. File it. A locality is not liable for interest on a refund for taxes you paid before you filed.
Manufactured homes qualify even if you do not own the land underneath. The home is exempt, but land you do not own is not.

The exemption also reaches property held as a life estate by you alone or with your spouse, property in a revocable inter vivos trust you or you and your spouse can revoke, and property in an irrevocable trust under which you hold a life estate or a continuing right of use or support. A leasehold or term of years is excluded, and a jointly owned property with non-qualifying owners is prorated by ownership percentage.

One acre is the floor, not always the ceiling. If your county, city, or town exempts or defers tax on more than one acre under its elderly and disabled program in Va. Code 58.1-3210, it must exempt the same number of acres for you.
Outbuildings on the exempt land are also exempt, so long as their main use is housing motor vehicles or household goods and it is not a business use. A detached garage counts.
This is administered by your local commissioner of the revenue or assessor, not by the state.
records.agency: Virginia counties, cities, and towns

records.title: Virginia income tax subtraction for military retirement and survivor benefits
records.summary: Virginia lets you subtract military retirement income from your state taxable income. For tax years beginning on or after January 1, 2025 the cap is $40,000, and there is no age requirement.
records.amount: Up to $40,000 of military benefits for tax years beginning on or after January 1, 2025. Up to $30,000 for tax year 2024.
eligibility: You receive military benefits as defined by the statute
For the 2024 and later subtraction there is no age requirement: it is allowed for an individual of any age
The earlier subtraction, covering tax years 2022 and 2023 at $10,000 and $20,000, was allowed only for an individual age 55 or older
You cannot claim this subtraction on income for which you already claimed another Virginia or federal credit, exemption, subtraction, or deduction
details: The statute defines military benefits as military retirement income for service in the Armed Forces, qualified military benefits under Internal Revenue Code Section 134, Survivor Benefit Plan payments to the surviving spouse of a Veteran, and military benefits paid to the surviving spouse of a Veteran.
Survivor Benefit Plan income counts. Surviving spouses often miss this.

Virginia also has a separate subtraction of up to $15,000 of military basic pay for members on extended active duty for more than 90 days. That one phases out dollar for dollar above $15,000 and disappears at $30,000 of basic pay. See the Virginia Department of Taxation military tax tips page.
A Congressional Medal of Honor recipient subtracts all military retirement income with no cap at all, under a separate provision of the same subdivision.

Military pay earned in a combat zone or a qualified hazardous duty area is subtracted in full under a different item of the same statute, so far as it is in your federal adjusted gross income and not already subtracted.
The cap amounts are set in statute by tax year. Check the current year figure on the Department of Taxation site before you file.
records.agency: Virginia Department of Taxation

records.title: Virginia Military Survivors and Dependents Education Program tuition waiver
records.summary: VMSDEP waives tuition and mandatory fees at Virginia public colleges for the spouse or child of a service member killed, missing, captured, or rated at least 90 percent permanently disabled from service. A separate fund can add money for room, board, and books.
records.amount: Waiver of tuition and mandatory fees at a Virginia public institution. Stipend of up to $2,000, or the amount set in the general appropriation act, for room and board, books and supplies, and other expenses.
eligibility: You are the spouse, or a child between the ages of 16 and 29, of a qualifying service member

The service member was killed, became missing in action, or became a prisoner of war while on active duty in the Armed Forces, the Reserves, or the Virginia National Guard during operations against terrorism, a peacekeeping mission, a terrorist act, or any armed conflict

Or the Veteran was rated by the U.S. Department of Veterans Affairs as totally and permanently disabled, or at least 90 percent permanently disabled, due to that service, and was discharged under conditions other than dishonorable
You must be admitted to a Virginia public institution of higher education and meet the domicile requirements in the statute
The Commissioner of Veterans Services may certify a dependent over age 29 where extenuating circumstances kept the child from using the benefit before age 30
details: The Commissioner of Veterans Services certifies eligibility. The waiver is applied by the school once you are admitted.

The domicile test looks at the service member, not the student. The service member must have established Virginia domicile at the time of entering active service or being called to active duty, or for a set period before, among other options in subsection C.
A stepchild counts as a child if the service member claimed the stepchild on a tax return or in DEERS while on active duty.

The stipend from the Virginia Military Survivors and Dependents Education Fund is separate from the waiver and is limited: combined with any other scholarship, grant, or waiver, it cannot exceed your actual allowed educational expenses. Each institution decides how the available fund money is distributed each year.

Funding rules for this program have been changed by the General Assembly more than once in recent years. Confirm the current stipend amount and any enrollment conditions with the Department of Veterans Services before you count on a figure.
records.agency: Virginia Department of Veterans Services

records.title: Service disabled Veteran-owned business certification and state contracting
records.summary: Virginia certifies small business owners as having service disabled Veteran status, and every public body must run a program to help service disabled Veteran-owned businesses win contracts. Awards to these businesses count toward agency contracting goals.
eligibility: You are a small business owner and you request the certification
For the business definition, at least 51 percent of the business or its equity ownership is owned by one or more service disabled Veterans
Both management and daily business operations are controlled by one or more service disabled Veterans

A service disabled Veteran served on active duty, was discharged or released under conditions other than dishonorable, and has a service-connected disability rating fixed by the U.S. Department of Veterans Affairs
details: The Department of Veterans Services adopts the regulations to certify service disabled Veteran status on request of the business owner, under Va. Code 2.2-2001 subsection D.

Under Va. Code 2.2-4310, no public body may discriminate against a bidder because of status as a service disabled Veteran, and public bodies must include businesses from the certified list kept by the Department of Small Business and Supplier Diversity when they solicit.

Contracts and subcontracts awarded to service disabled Veteran-owned businesses are credited toward the small business, women-owned business, and minority-owned business contracting and subcontracting goals of state agencies and their contractors. That gives agencies a reason to look for you.

Two agencies are involved. The Department of Veterans Services certifies the service disabled Veteran status. The Department of Small Business and Supplier Diversity maintains the vendor list public bodies must solicit from.
records.agency: Virginia Department of Veterans Services and Department of Small Business and Supplier Diversity

records.title: Burial in a state-operated Virginia Veterans cemetery
records.summary: The Commonwealth owns and operates Veterans cemeteries through the Department of Veterans Services. Burial vaults are provided at cost, and the state pays the burial fee for certain National Guard and Reserve members and for spouses.
eligibility: Virginia-domiciled Veterans and their spouses, orphans, and dependents, under guidelines the Department sets consistent with federal rules
The Commonwealth pays any burial fee charged for a member of the National Guard and Reserve buried at a state-operated Veterans cemetery
The Commonwealth also pays any burial fee for a deceased spouse of a member or Veteran of the Armed Forces or the National Guard and Reserve, whether the spouse dies before or after the member
Both of those fee payments depend on funds being appropriated or received for the purpose
details: Burial vaults are provided at cost to eligible Veterans and their family members interred at state-operated Veterans cemeteries. At cost, not free.

The Department of Veterans Services sets the eligibility guidelines, and the statute requires those guidelines to meet the intent of the federal statutes and regulations governing federal programs for Veterans and their spouses, orphans, and dependents.

These state cemeteries are separate from national cemeteries run by the U.S. Department of Veterans Affairs. Confirm locations, current fees, and pre-registration with the Department of Veterans Services.
Va. Code 2.2-2001 makes the Department responsible for operating and maintaining the Veterans cemeteries the Commonwealth owns.
records.agency: Virginia Department of Veterans Services

records.title: Virginia Veteran and Family Support: mental health and rehabilitation referrals
records.summary: Virginia runs a program that connects Veterans, transitioning service members, National Guard and Reserve members, and their families to mental health and rehabilitation services. Staff build a resource plan with you and check on your progress.
eligibility: Service members transitioning from military to civilian life
Veterans
Members of the Virginia National Guard
Virginia residents in the Armed Forces Reserves
Family members of any of the above
details: The Department of Veterans Services runs this with the Department of Behavioral Health and Developmental Services and the Department for Aging and Rehabilitative Services.

The statute directs the program to work with you on a coordinated resources plan that names the providers who can meet your needs, refer you to them, and then periodically monitor your progress toward the goals you identified.
Family members are included by statute. You do not have to be the Veteran to reach out.

Separately, Va. Code 2.2-2001 makes the Department of Veterans Services responsible for the medical care centers for Veterans that the Commonwealth owns and operates. These are state Veterans care centers offering skilled nursing and long term care. Contact the Department of Veterans Services for current locations, admission rules, and rates.
Program activity depends on the public and private funds appropriated for it.
records.agency: Virginia Department of Veterans Services

records.title: Veterans hiring preference for Commonwealth of Virginia jobs
records.summary: Virginia gives Veterans a hiring preference for state employment. On a written exam your score goes up by five percent, or by 10 percent if the VA has fixed a service-connected disability rating for you.
records.amount: Five percent added to a passing written exam score, or 10 percent with a service-connected disability rating
eligibility: You are a Veteran with an honorable discharge and the military service the statute specifies
The increase applies only if you pass the examination
A surviving spouse of a Veteran killed in the line of duty also gets the preference
A surviving child under age 27 of a Veteran killed in the line of duty also gets the preference
Members of the Virginia National Guard get a separate preference of five percentage points added to a passing assessment score
details: For state positions that are not based on passing an exam, a Veteran, surviving spouse, or child who meets all the knowledge, skill, and ability requirements is given preference during the selection process. Veterans with a disability rating get additional consideration.
The National Guard preference does not apply to a position limited to current state employees, and it does not apply if another applicant is a Veteran or a former prisoner of war.
This is preference, not a guarantee of hire. You still have to meet the posted requirements for the job.
records.agency: Commonwealth of Virginia state agencies

records.title: Reduced rate hunting and fishing licenses for Veterans with a disability
records.summary: Washington issues reduced rate combination fishing licenses and reduced rate hunting licenses to residents with a 30 percent or more service-connected disability. Nonresident Veterans with a disability pay what a nondisabled Washington resident pays.
records.amount: The statute sets the reduced combination fishing license rate at $6.90 and sets all hunting licenses at the reduced rate of a youth hunting license fee. Dealer and transaction fees may be added on top, so confirm the checkout total with WDFW.
eligibility: Washington resident with a 30 percent or more service-connected disability from military service
Or a Washington resident 65 or older with a qualifying military discharge and a service-connected disability
The same reduced rates in this statute also cover residents who use a wheelchair, residents who are blind or visually impaired, and residents with a documented developmental disability
A written application is required
details: The statute text reads: 'Upon written application, a combination fishing license shall be issued at the reduced rate of $6.90 and all hunting licenses shall be issued at the reduced rate of a youth hunting license fee'.

For nonresidents the statute provides that upon department verification of eligibility, a nonstate resident Veteran with a disability who otherwise satisfies the criteria must be issued a combination fishing license or any hunting license at the same cost charged to a nondisabled Washington resident for the same license.
The same section provides free small game, big game, and migratory bird permits to State Guard and National Guard members, full time or participating in part time drills.

The dollar figure above is the amount written in the statute. Fees can be changed by the legislature, so verify the current price with the Washington Department of Fish and Wildlife before you budget for it.
You will need documentation of your VA rating when you apply.
records.agency: Washington Department of Fish and Wildlife

records.title: Disabled American Veteran and former prisoner of war license plates
records.summary: Washington issues Disabled American Veteran and former prisoner of war plates for one personal use vehicle with no vehicle license fees, license plate fees, or excise taxes. A qualifying Veteran can instead keep regular plates and still get the same fee and tax exemption.
records.amount: One personal use vehicle is issued without payment of any vehicle license fees, license plate fees, or excise taxes.
eligibility: You are a Veteran as defined in RCW 41.04.007 and are the recorded registered owner of the vehicle

The statute lists five qualifying paths: certification from the VA or your military service that you have a service-connected disability rating; loss of use of both hands or one foot; capture and incarceration by an enemy during a period of war with the United States plus receipt of a prisoner of war medal; blindness in both eyes as a result of military service; or being rated and receiving service-connected compensation at the 100 percent rate that is expected to exist for more than one year
The vehicle must be a personal use motor vehicle required to display one or two plates, excluding vehicles registered under chapter 46.87 RCW
The exemption does not apply to commercially registered or commercially used vehicles
details: The Department of Licensing's published requirement is an eligibility letter from the US Department of Veterans Affairs verifying a 100 percent VA disability rating expected to last more than one year, which is narrower than the full list of paths in the statute. If you qualify under one of the other statutory paths, raise it with DOL directly rather than assuming you are ineligible.
Under subsection (3) you may skip the special plate and apply for regular issue or any qualifying special plate while still receiving the full vehicle license fee and excise tax exemption.
DOL states these plates cover motorcycles, motor homes, passenger vehicles, and trucks in personal use, regardless of gross weight, and that the plates do not need to be renewed.
The plates may be transferred to another motor vehicle you own by applying to DOL, a county auditor, an agent, or a subagent.
Disabled American Veteran plates cannot be personalized.
The department may periodically verify the 100 percent rate.
Unauthorized use of one of these plates is a gross misdemeanor.
Apply by mail with your VA eligibility letter and the Military Services and Veterans License Plate Application, with the disabled American veteran plates or tabs box checked.
records.agency: Washington State Department of Licensing

records.title: Property tax exemption for Veterans with a service-connected disability
records.summary: Washington exempts part of the property tax on a Veteran's primary residence, based on VA disability rating and household income. The rating requirement has been lowered, and the state's own benefit page has not caught up, so read the statute rather than the agency page.
records.amount: Depends on your income tier. Through tax year 2026 the lowest tier exempts regular property taxes on the greater of $60,000 or 60 percent of the valuation, and the middle tier the greater of $50,000 or 35 percent capped at $70,000. Both rise for 2027. See the details.
eligibility: You own and occupy the residence as your principal place of residence in Washington at the time of filing
You are a Veteran of the armed forces entitled to and receiving compensation from the US Department of Veterans Affairs
You qualify with a total disability rating for a service-connected disability, without regard to evaluation percent

Or you qualify by combined service-connected evaluation rating. RCW 84.36.381 as it currently stands sets that at 40 percent or higher. The Department of Revenue's benefit page still states 80 percent. See the details below before you assume you do not qualify
Your combined disposable income must be at or below one of three county-specific income thresholds

There is no minimum age on the Veteran pathway. A surviving spouse or surviving domestic partner of a person who was receiving the exemption when they died qualifies at 57 or older if they otherwise meet the requirements

You may own in fee, as a life estate, or by contract purchase, or hold a share in a cooperative housing association representing your unit. A lease for life counts as a life estate, and a residence owned by a marital community, a registered domestic partnership, or cotenants is treated as owned by each of them
details: This one is genuinely in motion and the sources disagree, so here is what each says. RCW 84.36.381(3)(a)(ii), as published today by the Legislature, requires a combined service-connected evaluation rating of 40 percent or higher, or a total disability rating without regard to evaluation percent. The Department of Revenue's exemption page still says 80 percent, or compensation at the 100 percent rate.

The likely explanation is timing. Both amending acts, chapter 200 of the Laws of 2025 and chapter 163 of the Laws of 2026, carry the same applicability note: they apply to taxes levied for collection in 2027 and thereafter. So 80 percent governed taxes collected in 2026, and the lower figure governs from the 2027 collection year, which is what you are applying for now.

The 2025 act was titled as a phase down of the rating requirement. The 2026 act amended the same section again, and the text the Legislature publishes today shows a single 40 percent figure rather than a year by year schedule.

Do not take this from us. If your rating is between 40 and 79 percent, ask your county assessor directly which rating applies to the year you are filing for, and say that you are asking about RCW 84.36.381 as amended by chapter 163 of the Laws of 2026. A Veteran who reads the Department of Revenue page alone would conclude they do not qualify.

Income thresholds are not fixed dollar figures statewide. RCW 84.36.383 sets them as the greater of the prior year threshold or a percentage of county median household income, so the cutoff differs by county. The Department of Revenue calculates and publishes county-specific thresholds every three years. The 2027 tax year figures are published now, and the next adjustment is for tax year 2030.

The percentages themselves went up. For tax years 2024 through 2026 the thresholds were 50, 60 and 70 percent of county median household income. For 2027 and after they are 60, 70 and 80 percent, so more Veterans clear them.
Combat-related special compensation is excluded from combined disposable income under the 2026 act. If CRSC was counted against you before, that changes your arithmetic.

At the top income tier the exemption covers excess property taxes, the state property tax under RCW 84.52.065, and certain voter-approved levy portions. The two lower tiers also get the regular property tax exemption in the amount field above.

Qualifying freezes the valuation used for the exemption at the assessed value on the later of 1 January 1995 or 1 January of the assessment year you first qualified. Later improvements are added at their true and fair value.

Being away from home does not necessarily cost you the exemption. Confinement to a hospital, nursing home, assisted living facility, adult family home, or a relative's home for long-term care is fine if the residence is temporarily unoccupied, is lived in by your spouse or domestic partner or someone financially dependent on you, or is rented out to pay for that care.
If you sell, transfer, or are displaced from the home, you may move your exemption status to a replacement residence. No claimant may hold the exemption on more than one residence in a year.
You apply through your county assessor, not the state. Renewal is required periodically as determined by the local assessor.
records.agency: Washington State Department of Revenue, administered by county assessors
records.statuteRef: RCW 84.36.379 through 84.36.389, amended by 2025 c 200 s 1

records.title: Washington has no state personal income tax on military pay or retired pay
records.summary: The Department of Revenue states that Washington does not currently have an individual income tax. Active duty pay, military retired pay, VA disability compensation, and survivor benefits are therefore not taxed by the state.
records.amount: No state personal income tax is currently imposed on any wage, retirement, or benefit income.
eligibility: This applies to every Washington resident, so there is no Veteran specific filing, form, or subtraction to claim
You do not file a Washington personal income tax return
details: The Department of Revenue's income tax page states: "Washington does not currently have an individual income tax."

That is changing at the top end. The 2026 Legislature passed Senate Bill 6346, creating a 9.9 percent income tax on individuals and married couples filing jointly with annual adjusted gross income above $1 million. It takes effect 1 January 2028 and the first returns are due in April 2029.
For almost every Veteran this changes nothing. A million dollars of adjusted gross income is far above military retired pay, and VA disability compensation is not in adjusted gross income at all.
Revenue says it will keep updating that page as filing requirements, forms, and administration are worked out, so check it rather than relying on this if the threshold could reach you.
You still owe federal income tax. Military retired pay is federally taxable. VA disability compensation is not.
Washington raises revenue through sales tax, business and occupation tax, and property tax instead, so no income tax does not mean a low overall tax burden.
records.agency: Washington State Department of Revenue

records.title: Property tax and special assessment deferral for homeowners with limited income
records.summary: Washington lets qualifying homeowners postpone paying property taxes and special assessments on their residence. The state pays the county on your behalf and records a lien that is repaid later, typically when the home is sold or transferred.
records.amount: Deferral is allowed on up to 80 percent of the claimant's equity value in the residence.
eligibility: You must be 60 years of age or older on December 31 of the year the deferral claim is filed, or you must have been, at the time of filing, retired from regular gainful employment by reason of disability as defined in RCW 84.36.383
You must meet all the requirements of the RCW 84.36.381 exemption apart from its age and income limits
Your combined disposable income must be at or below the deferral income threshold, which is set as a percentage of county median household income

You must own the residence where the taxes are imposed. A share in cooperative housing, a life estate, a lease for life, or a revocable trust does not satisfy the ownership test for the deferral, even though some of those do satisfy it for the exemption
You must keep fire and casualty insurance in force covering the state's interest in your equity value
A surviving spouse, surviving domestic partner, heir, or devisee of a person who was receiving a deferral at death qualifies at 57 or older if they otherwise meet the requirements
details: This is a general low income program, not a Veteran specific one. Chapter 84.38 RCW does not create a separate Veteran category. A Veteran under 60 who is not retired from gainful employment by reason of disability will not qualify for the deferral even if that Veteran qualifies for the RCW 84.36.381 exemption. The two programs are easy to conflate and the age gate is the difference.

Deferral is not forgiveness. The deferred amount becomes a lien in favor of the state with priority over most other liens, and interest accrues on the balance. Confirm the current interest rate with your county assessor or the Department of Revenue before you rely on any figure.
The ownership rules are stricter than the exemption's. If you hold your home through a revocable trust or a life estate, you can take the exemption but not the deferral.
If you let the fire and casualty insurance lapse, the amount you may defer is cut to no more than 100 percent of your equity value in the land or lot only.

The deferral income threshold is the greater of the previous year's threshold or 75 percent of county median household income for tax years 2020 through 2026, rising to 90 percent for tax year 2027 and after.
For a special assessment deferral, you must have opted to pay that assessment on the installment method where that method was available.
You file a written declaration with your county assessor.
The deferral can be combined with the exemption. Many claimants take the exemption first, then defer what is still owed.
records.agency: Washington State Department of Revenue, filed with county assessors

records.title: Washington State Veterans Cemetery at Medical Lake
records.summary: Washington operates a state Veterans cemetery in Medical Lake, west of Spokane, for honorably discharged Veterans and eligible family members. There is no direct charge for interment of a Veteran or service member.
records.amount: No direct charge for interment of a Veteran or military member. WDVA published a $311 charge for interment or memorialization of a family member effective October 1, 2025, which cannot be prepaid and is adjusted annually based on the consumer price index. Confirm the current figure before you plan.
eligibility: Open to members of the armed forces who have met a minimum active duty service requirement and were discharged under conditions other than dishonorable
Spouses, state registered domestic partners, widows and widowers, and minor dependent children may also be eligible
Unmarried adult children with disabilities may be eligible in certain circumstances
The statute ties eligibility to the federal standards in 38 C.F.R. Sec. 38.620
details: The cemetery is at 21702 West Espanola Road, Medical Lake, WA 99022, about three miles west of Fairchild Air Force Base.

RCW 72.36.115 directs WDVA to establish and maintain an eastern Washington state Veterans cemetery and to adopt rules defining services, eligibility, fees, and general operations. Fee details live in rule and on WDVA's site, not in the statute.
Interment options include casketed remains and cremated remains, with casket burial sites, columbarium niches, in-ground cremation inurnment, and a scattering garden.
WDVA describes interment as an earned federal benefit and submits VA plot allowance claims directly, or Department of Defense claims for service members, rather than billing the family.
Washington Veterans are also entitled to interment at Tahoma National Cemetery. The state cemetery was created to give eastern Washington families a closer option.
You can request a pre-need eligibility determination from WDVA rather than leaving it to your family. Cemetery phone: (509) 299-6280.
records.agency: Washington State Department of Veterans Affairs

records.title: Washington State Veterans Homes long term and nursing care
records.summary: Washington operates four state Veterans homes offering 24 hour nursing care, medical care, and pharmacy services to Veterans, and in some cases to spouses, surviving spouses, and Gold Star parents.
eligibility: Applicants must be actual bona fide residents of Washington at the time of application
Served at any time in any branch of the United States armed forces, including the National Guard, per WDVA's published criteria
Received an honorable discharge, or are already eligible for federal Department of Veterans Affairs monetary benefits
The statute also covers members of the state militia disabled while on duty, and Filipino World War II Veterans who served with American forces

Spouses and domestic partners may be admitted, with a requirement in the statute that they were married to and living with the Veteran for three years before application, or were residents of a state Veterans home if married afterward
Parents of a child who died in military service may also be admitted
All applicants must apply for all federal and state benefits for which they may be eligible, including medical assistance under chapter 74.09 RCW
details: The four homes are the Washington Soldiers Home in Orting, the Washington Veterans Home in Port Orchard also known as Retsil, the Spokane Veterans Home, and the Walla Walla Veterans Home.

WDVA states the homes are Medicare and Medicaid certified and provide 24 hour nursing care, medical care, and pharmacy services, along with physical and occupational therapy, recreation, social services, hospice, and religious programs.

Cost is not free. The statute contemplates that resident income is deposited and applied, and requires applicants to pursue federal and state benefits first. Ask the admissions team for a written explanation of what you will owe before you sign anything.
RCW 73.04.140 bars the WDVA director and department employees from serving as guardian for a home resident.
Call the admission team at 1-877-838-7787 to arrange a tour and start an application.
records.agency: Washington State Department of Veterans Affairs

records.title: Tuition and fee waivers at Washington public colleges for Veterans and their families
records.summary: Washington public universities and community and technical colleges must waive all tuition and fees for the children and spouses of Veterans who became totally disabled, died in service, or are POW or MIA. They may waive tuition for other eligible Veterans and Guard members.
records.amount: Full tuition and fees for the required waiver. Total credits earned using the waiver may not exceed 250 quarter credits or the semester equivalent. A textbook and course materials stipend of $500 per academic year is also provided, subject to amounts appropriated.
eligibility: Required full waiver: a child, spouse, domestic partner, or surviving spouse or surviving domestic partner of an eligible Veteran or National Guard member who became totally disabled as a result of active federal military or naval service, or who is federally determined to be a prisoner of war or missing in action

Required full waiver: a child or surviving spouse or surviving domestic partner of an eligible Veteran or National Guard member who lost his or her life as a result of active federal military or naval service
A child must be a Washington domiciliary between 17 and 26 years old. Marital status does not affect eligibility

A surviving spouse or surviving domestic partner must be a Washington domiciliary and has 10 years to use the waiver, running from the latest of the date of death, the date of total disability, or the federal determination of service-connected death, total disability, or POW or MIA status
Remarriage or registration in a subsequent domestic partnership ends eligibility for the required waiver

Permissive waiver: the governing boards may waive all or a portion of tuition and fees for an eligible Veteran or National Guard member, and separately for a Washington domiciliary Veteran who did not serve on foreign soil or in international waters
details: 'Eligible veteran or national guard member' is defined in the statute as a Washington domiciliary who served in active federal service under Title 10 or Title 32 in a war or conflict fought on foreign soil or in international waters, or in support of those serving there, and who has a qualifying discharge as defined in RCW 73.04.005.
'Totally disabled' means a person determined to be 100 percent disabled by the federal Department of Veterans Affairs.

Waivers under subsection (3) for Veterans who did not serve on foreign soil carry no state general fund support, so whether a school offers them depends on that school's budget. Ask the campus directly.
Graduate tuition waivers are not required for those who qualify, but the statute encourages them.
Recipients may attend full time or part time, and continued participation is subject to the school's satisfactory progress policy.
Private vocational schools and private higher education institutions are encouraged, not required, to offer comparable waivers.
Apply through the financial aid or Veteran services office at the Washington public college or university you plan to attend.
records.agency: Governing boards of the state universities, regional universities, The Evergreen State College, and the community and technical colleges

records.title: Veterans scoring criteria and hiring preference in Washington public employment
records.summary: Washington adds a percentage to a Veteran's passing score on competitive examinations for state, county, and municipal jobs. Veterans also receive preference in appointment to public departments and on state and county public works.
records.amount: 10 percent added to a passing score for service during a period of war or armed conflict. 5 percent otherwise. 5 percent on promotional examinations for those called to active service from public employment.
eligibility: You are a Veteran as defined in RCW 41.04.007, or a member of the uniformed services as defined in RCW 41.04.010
You have a qualifying discharge as defined in RCW 73.04.005, shown by a DD Form 214, NGB Form 22, or equivalent successor discharge paperwork
A predischarge certification may be used if issued no more than 120 days before submission, with official discharge documentation supplied within 30 days after discharge
Under RCW 73.16.010 the preference also reaches spouses of active duty service members and spouses of Veterans with a disability
details: The 10 percent applies to a Veteran or uniformed service member who served during a period of war or in an armed conflict as defined in RCW 41.04.005 and who does not receive military retirement.
The 5 percent applies to a Veteran or uniformed service member who did not serve during a period of war or armed conflict, or who is receiving military retirement.
The 10 percent and the general 5 percent are added until your first appointment and may not be used in promotional examinations.

The separate 5 percent for someone called to active military service from employment with the state or a political subdivision or municipal corporation applies to promotional examinations, and only until the first promotion.
The percentage is added to a passing mark, grade, or rating only, based on a possible rating of 100 points as perfect. It does not turn a failing score into a passing one.
RCW 73.16.010 separately provides that a physical impairment that does not prevent you from performing the job's duties is not a disqualifying factor.
You must claim the preference. Ask the hiring agency how, and be ready to attach your discharge document.
records.agency: Washington state agencies, counties, cities, and municipal corporations, plus contractors administering their examinations

records.title: Veterans Estate Management Program fiduciary and protective payee services
records.summary: WDVA can serve as VA fiduciary, Social Security representative payee, or executor for Veterans and their dependents who cannot manage their own finances, making sure income goes to housing, food, clothing, and medical care.
eligibility: The statute covers an incapacitated Veteran or an incapacitated Veteran's dependent who is a Washington resident and whose federal benefits are tied to a fiduciary appointment
WDVA may act when no responsible family member is available to serve
The director may also act as executor of a deceased Veteran's estate where no executor has been designated
details: RCW 73.04.130 authorizes the director to implement a veteran estate management program and to petition for appointment as fiduciary or executor, serving without bond.
The statute preserves existing rights of succession under other law and respects designations made in a Veteran's will.

WDVA describes the program as protective payee services: making timely payments to clients and vendors for housing, food, clothing, and medical care, protecting client assets from creditor claims and financial loss, and helping clients access all available federal and state benefits.
RCW 73.04.140 prohibits the director or any other department employee from serving as guardian for a resident of the Washington state Veterans homes.
WDVA did not publish a fee schedule for this program. Ask what, if anything, is deducted before you enroll.
Contact 1-800-562-2308 or 360-485-1807, or write to the Washington State Department of Veterans Affairs, 1102 Quince St. SE, PO Box 41150, Olympia, WA 98504-1150.
records.agency: Washington State Department of Veterans Affairs

records.title: Veterans Innovations Program emergency financial assistance
records.summary: The Washington State Department of Veterans Affairs runs the Veterans Innovations Program to provide crisis and emergency relief plus education, training, and employment assistance to post 9/11 Veterans, National Guard members, and reservists facing financial hardship.
eligibility: Washington resident
Served on or after September 11, 2001

Served honorably, or are already eligible for federal Department of Veterans Affairs monetary benefits, or were separated with a less than honorable characterization of service due solely to sexual orientation, gender identity, or gender expression, or to actions or statements related to them, regardless of characterization of service
Is experiencing financial hardship where income is not sufficient to meet basic needs
Presents a discernable positive outcome
Request is within the grant funding capabilities
A complete application with required documentation must be submitted
details: RCW 43.60A.160 directs the department to provide funding for crisis and emergency relief and for education, training, and employment assistance to eligible Veterans, National Guard members, and armed forces reserves.
WDVA reports the program has been used for employment transition, homelessness and eviction or foreclosure prevention, education transition, utility shutoff prevention, and transportation needs.

The program is funded from the Veterans Innovations Program account under RCW 43.60A.185 and awards depend on available funding, so there is no entitlement. Apply early rather than at the last moment.
WDVA did not publish a maximum award or lifetime limit on its program page. Ask before you count on a specific amount.
Submit the VIP application to wdvavip@dva.wa.gov, or call 1-800-562-2308.
records.agency: Washington State Department of Veterans Affairs
